title: Clique immersion conjecture
open: Does every \(t\)-chromatic graph contain a weak immersion of \(K_t\), with distinct branch vertices connected by pairwise edge-disjoint paths?
status: Open since the late twentieth century. Fox–Pach–Suk establish the conclusion when the graph has at most \((1.64-o(1))t\) vertices.
why: Would force complete communication patterns from chromatic complexity.
key_works: Fox–Pach–Suk (2025), [*Immersions and Albertson’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05893).

title: Thomassen’s large-girth, large-minimum-degree conjecture
open: For every \(k,g\), does sufficiently large minimum degree force a subgraph with minimum degree at least \(k\) and girth at least \(g\)?
status: Proposed in 1983. Important bounded-girth cases are known; the general statement remains open.
why: Would extract locally sparse structure while retaining substantial connectivity.
key_works: Christoph–Janzer–Petrova–Steiner (2025), [*Extending Thomassen’s conjecture to directed graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11311).

title: Reed’s chromatic-number conjecture
open: Prove \(\chi(G)\le\lceil(\Delta(G)+1+\omega(G))/2\rceil\) for every graph.
status: Proposed in 1998. Weaker universal interpolation bounds and many exact special cases are known.
why: Would sharply combine maximum degree and clique obstructions.
key_works: Reed (1998), [*ω, Δ, and χ*](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/%28SICI%291097-0118%28199804%2927%3A4%3C177%3A%3AAID-JGT1%3E3.0.CO%3B2-K).

title: Total coloring conjecture
open: Color all vertices and edges of every simple graph with at most \(\Delta+2\) colors, respecting every adjacency and incidence conflict.
status: Proposed independently in the 1960s. Numerous classes are settled; dense-graph results do not cover the unrestricted case.
why: Gives the fundamental simultaneous node-and-link scheduling bound.
key_works: Henderschedt–McDonald–Shan (2025), [*Total coloring graphs with large minimum degree*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.05548).

title: Equitable list-coloring conjecture
open: If \(\Delta(G)\le r-1\), do arbitrary lists of \(r\) colors permit a proper coloring using each color at most \(\lceil |V(G)|/r\rceil\) times?
status: Proposed in 2003. Ordinary equitable coloring is settled; the unrestricted list version remains open.
why: Combines individual eligibility with balanced workloads.
key_works: Kostochka–Pelsmajer–West (2003), [*A list analogue of equitable coloring*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.10137).

title: Cereceda’s quadratic recoloring conjecture
open: Connect any two proper \((d+2)\)-colorings of an \(n\)-vertex \(d\)-degenerate graph by \(O_d(n^2)\) valid single-vertex recolorings.
status: Open since 2007. A general \(O(n^{d+1})\) bound is known; quadratic bounds hold with additional slack or restrictions.
why: Bounds the cost of moving between feasible configurations.
key_works: Bousquet–Heinrich (2019), [*A polynomial version of Cereceda’s conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.05619).

title: Fan–Raspaud conjecture
subfield: Flows, perfect matchings, and cycle covers
open: Does every bridgeless cubic graph have three perfect matchings with empty common intersection?
status: Proposed in 1994; implied by Berge–Fulkerson. Numerous special cases are known.
why: Isolates a weaker matching-compatibility obstruction.
key_works: Karabáš–Máčajová–Nedela–Škoviera (2026), [*Regular colouring defect of a cubic graph and the conjectures of Fan–Raspaud and Fulkerson*](https://doi.org/10.26493/1855-3974.3291.A20).

title: Barnette’s conjecture
open: Prove that every 3-connected cubic bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
status: Proposed in 1969. Special face-size cases and strong approximate Hamiltonian structures are known.
why: Would force spanning tours from planarity, regularity, and connectivity.
key_works: Bekos–Kaufmann–Pfister (2025), [*Approximating Barnette’s Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.GD.2025.6).

title: Sheehan’s conjecture
open: Prove that no finite simple 4-regular graph has exactly one Hamiltonian cycle.
status: Proposed in 1975. Odd-degree parity arguments and extensive searches leave the 4-regular case open.
why: Would force multiple spanning tours from modest uniform redundancy.
key_works: Sheehan (1977), [*Graphs with exactly one hamiltonian circuit*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.3190010110); Brinkmann–De Pauw (2024), [*Uniquely hamiltonian graphs for many sets of degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.08946).

title: Chvátal’s toughness conjecture
open: Is there a universal \(t\) such that every \(t\)-tough graph is Hamiltonian, where \(|S|\ge t\,c(G-S)\) whenever \(c(G-S)>1\)?
status: Open since 1973. Numerous forbidden-induced-subgraph classes admit sufficient toughness constants.
why: Tests whether bounded strengthening of the separation obstruction captures Hamiltonicity.
key_works: Shan (2025), [*Hamiltonian cycles in tough \((P_4\cup P_1)\)-free graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08936).

title: Matthews–Sumner conjecture
open: Prove that every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamiltonian.
status: Proposed in 1984. Every 7-connected claw-free graph is Hamilton-connected; connectivity four remains open.
why: Would turn a local branching prohibition into a sharp spanning-cycle guarantee.
key_works: Ryjáček–Vrána (2011), [*Line graphs of multigraphs and Hamilton-connectedness of claw-free graphs*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jgt.20498).
aliases: Equivalent to Thomassen’s 4-connected line-graph Hamiltonicity conjecture.

title: Classification of 2-factor-Hamiltonian cubic bipartite braces
open: Are \(K_{3,3}\) and the Heawood graph the only cubic bipartite braces in which every 2-factor is Hamiltonian?
status: The Pfaffian case was settled in 2025; non-Pfaffian braces remain.
why: Classifies graphs where every spanning degree-two structure is connected.
key_works: Gorsky–Johanni–Wiederrecht (2025), [*A note on the 2-Factor Hamiltonicity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08128).

title: Graceful tree conjecture
open: Label every \(n\)-vertex tree bijectively by \(0,\ldots,n-1\), so its edge differences are exactly \(1,\ldots,n-1\).
status: Rosa, 1967. Many families are settled; recent gracesize results obtain almost all required differences.
why: Produces structured cyclic decompositions with no repeated differences.
key_works: Letzter–Pokrovskiy–Williams (2025–2026), [*On the gracesize of trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.11331).

title: Tree packing conjecture
open: Pack arbitrary trees \(T_i\) with \(|V(T_i)|=i\), \(1\le i\le n\), edge-disjointly into \(K_n\).
status: Proposed in 1976. Almost-linear maximum-degree cases are known; an unrestricted claimed proof was withdrawn in September 2026.
why: Would show that tree orders alone suffice for complete coordinated packing.
key_works: Allen et al., [*The tree packing conjecture for trees of almost linear maximum degree*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11720); Chalise–Clark–Gnang, [withdrawn proof](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13840).

title: Gallai’s path decomposition conjecture
open: Partition every connected \(n\)-vertex graph’s edges into at most \(\lceil n/2\rceil\) simple paths.
status: Open since the 1960s. Planar graphs, maximum degree at most five, and further classes are settled.
why: Gives an optimal universal bound on nonrepeating route decompositions.
key_works: Chu–Fan–Zhou (2026), [*Gallai’s conjecture and the path number of odd semi-cliques*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2025.114725).

title: Codegree threshold for a tetrahedron
open: Prove that minimum pair-degree greater than \((1/2+\varepsilon)n\) forces \(K_4^{(3)}\) in sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraphs.
status: Matching lower constructions exist. The analogous threshold for \(K_4^{(3)}\) minus an edge is settled; the complete tetrahedron remains open.
why: Measures how local pair abundance forces global consistency.
key_works: Falgas-Ravry–Pikhurko–Vaughan–Volec (2023), [*The codegree threshold of \(K_4^-\)*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.12722).

title: Brown–Erdős–Sós sparse-configuration conjecture
open: For each \(k\ge3\), must every 3-uniform hypergraph with \(\varepsilon n^2\) edges contain \(k\) edges spanning at most \(k+3\) vertices?
status: Proposed in 1973. The \(k=3\) case is the Ruzsa–Szemerédi theorem; four edges on seven vertices is the first unresolved case.
why: Connects sparse hypergraphs to removal and recurrence phenomena.
key_works: Brown–Erdős–Sós (1973), *On the existence of triangulated spheres in 3-graphs, and related problems*; [Erdős’ problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TripleSystems.html).

title: Erdős’ girth conjecture
open: For every fixed \(k\ge2\), construct arbitrarily large graphs with girth greater than \(2k\) and \(\Omega(n^{1+1/k})\) edges.
status: The upper exponent follows from breadth-first expansion. Matching constructions are known for selected parameters, including \(k=2,3,5\).
why: Would determine the optimal density of graphs without short cycles.
key_works: Parter (2014), [*Bypassing Erdős’ Girth Conjecture: Hybrid Stretch and Sourcewise Spanners*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6835).

title: Meyniel’s cop-number conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove that \(O(\sqrt n)\) cops suffice to capture one robber on every connected \(n\)-vertex graph in the standard perfect-information game.
status: Proposed in the 1980s. The scale is necessary; random graphs satisfy the conjecture, but the universal bound remains open.
why: Determines the sharp universal pursuit resource requirement.
key_works: Prałat–Wormald (2016), [*Meyniel’s conjecture holds for random graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.2841).

title: Harary–Hill crossing-number conjecture
subfield: Graph parameters and topological graph theory
open: Prove \(\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=\frac14\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-3)/2\rfloor\).
status: Proposed in the 1960s. Matching drawings exist; the lower bound is known for substantial restricted drawing classes.
why: Determines unavoidable crossings in complete interconnection networks.
key_works: Ábrego–Aichholzer–Fernández-Merchant–Ramos–Salazar (2013), [*Shellable drawings and the cylindrical crossing number of \(K_n\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3665).

title: Leading constant in \(R(3,t)\)
open: Determine whether \(R(3,t)\sim c\,t^2/\log t\), and find \(c\).
status: The order was settled in 1995. A 2025–2026 preprint raises the lower constant to \(1/2\); the upper constant remains one.
why: Would precisely quantify triangle-free graphs with bounded independence number.
key_works: Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender, [*Improving \(R(3,k)\) in just two bites*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19718).

title: Polynomial superlinearity for bounded-degree size-Ramsey numbers
open: Do fixed \(\Delta,\varepsilon>0\) permit \(n\)-vertex maximum-degree-\(\Delta\) graphs with size-Ramsey number at least \(n^{1+\varepsilon}\)?
status: Linear growth is false. Known subcubic constructions require \(n\exp(c\sqrt{\log n})\), still subpolynomial above linear.
why: Tests whether bounded local complexity can force polynomial hosting overhead.
key_works: Tikhomirov (2024), [*On bounded degree graphs with large size-Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.05818).

title: Ramsey multiplicity constant of \(K_4\)
open: Determine the minimum asymptotic proportion of monochromatic four-vertex cliques in red–blue complete graphs.
status: Thomason refuted the random-coloring value \(1/32\) in 1989. Current constructions and lower bounds do not coincide.
why: Measures unavoidable abundance beyond Ramsey existence.
key_works: Parczyk–Pokutta–Spiegel–Szabó (2025), [*New Ramsey Multiplicity Bounds and Search Heuristics*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04036).

title: Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture
open: Must every \(n\)-vertex digraph of minimum outdegree at least \(r\) contain a directed cycle of length at most \(\lceil n/r\rceil\)?
status: Proposed in 1978. Even the exact triangle threshold near \(n/3\) remains open.
why: Would infer short feedback loops from one-sided expansion.
key_works: Aharoni–Berger–Chudnovsky–Guo–Zerbib (2021), [*Non-uniform degrees and rainbow versions of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.11183).

title: Hoàng–Reed directed cactus conjecture
open: Does minimum outdegree \(d\) force directed cycles \(C_1,\ldots,C_d\), each meeting the preceding union in at most one vertex?
status: Proposed in the 1980s; the cases through \(d=3\) are known.
why: Would produce tightly controlled branching arrangements of directed cycles.
key_works: Welhan (2010), [*The Hoàng–Reed Conjecture for \(\delta^+=3\)*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2010.03.001).

title: Neumann-Lara’s planar dichromatic conjecture
open: Partition every oriented planar graph’s vertices into two sets inducing acyclic digraphs.
status: Proposed in 1985. Many girth-restricted cases are settled; arbitrary planar orientations remain open.
why: Would bound planar directed cyclic complexity by two layers.
key_works: Steiner (2019), [*A Note on Graphs of Dichromatic Number 2*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00351).

title: Erdős–Turán additive-basis conjecture
open: If \(A\subseteq\mathbb N_0\) represents every sufficiently large integer as \(a+b\), prove that the ordered representation counts are unbounded.
status: Posed in 1941. Fixed lower bounds, including eight, do not establish unboundedness.
why: Would rule out uniformly sparse representations in an additive basis.
key_works: Borwein–Choi–Chu (2006), [*An old conjecture of Erdős–Turán on additive bases*](https://www.sfu.ca/~schoia/paper/erdos.pdf).
prize: Historical Erdős offer: US$500; current administration unverified.

title: Sharp four-term progression bounds
open: Determine the asymptotic scale of \(r_4(N)\).
status: Density convergence was proved in 1969. The verified benchmark is \(r_4(N)\ll N(\log N)^{-c}\), far from constructions.
why: Isolates the first major quantitative gap involving quadratic structure.
key_works: Green–Tao (2017), [*New bounds for Szemerédi’s theorem, III: A polylogarithmic bound for \(r_4(N)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01703).

title: Sharp Szemerédi bounds for longer progressions
open: Determine the correct asymptotic scale of \(r_k(N)\) for each fixed \(k\ge5\).
status: Existence settled in 1975. Leng–Sah–Sawhney give \(N\exp[-(\log\log N)^{c_k}]\); a large gap remains.
why: Would make higher-order Fourier analysis quantitatively predictive.
key_works: Leng–Sah–Sawhney (2024), [*Improved Bounds for Szemerédi’s Theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17995).

title: Sharp corners bounds
open: Determine the maximum size of \(A\subset[N]^2\) avoiding \((x,y),(x+d,y),(x,y+d)\), \(d\ne0\).
status: Ajtai–Szemerédi, 1974. A 2025 theorem gives density at most \(\exp[-(\log N)^{\Omega(1)}]\).
why: Connects multidimensional avoidance to communication complexity.
key_works: Jaber–Liu–Lovett–Ostuni–Sawhney (2025), [*Quasipolynomial bounds for the corners theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07006).

title: Quantitative density Hales–Jewett
open: Determine the least dimension \(N(k,\delta)\) forcing a combinatorial line in every density-\(\delta\) subset of \([k]^N\).
status: Existence was proved in 1991. For three letters, Polymath gives a tower of height \(O(\delta^{-3})\); matching scales are remote.
why: Quantifies a foundational density and recurrence principle.
key_works: D. H. J. Polymath (2009/2012), [*A new proof of the density Hales–Jewett theorem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.3926).

title: Hindman’s mixed sum–product quadruple
open: Must every finite coloring of \(\mathbb N\) contain distinct \(x,y\) with \(x,y,x+y,xy\) all the same color?
status: Posed in 1979. Two colors and rational-number analogues are settled; arbitrary finite natural-number colorings remain open.
why: Requires simultaneous additive and multiplicative recurrence.
key_works: Richter (2025/2026), [*Sums and products in sets of positive density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00515).

title: Arbitrarily large finite sums-and-products configurations
open: For every finite coloring of \(\mathbb N\) and every \(k\), find \(k\) distinct numbers whose nonempty subset sums and products are all one color.
status: Hindman, 1979. The rational analogue is proved; requiring one infinite set is false.
why: Tests the extent of compatibility between two algebraic operations.
key_works: Alweiss (2023/2026), [*Monochromatic Sums and Products over \(\mathbb Q\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08901); Richter, [density approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00515).

title: Chvátal’s hereditary-family conjecture
open: In every finite hereditary family containing a nonempty set, is some maximum intersecting subfamily a star?
status: Proposed in 1974. Many structured hereditary families are settled; the unrestricted nonuniform case remains open.
why: Extends Erdős–Ko–Rado to arbitrary down-sets.
key_works: Chvátal (1974), *Intersecting families of edges in hypergraphs having the hereditary property*; Kupavskii (2023), [uniform hereditary families](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02246).

title: Additive-square avoidance
open: Does an infinite word over some finite integer alphabet avoid every pair of consecutive equal-length, equal-sum blocks?
status: Posed around 2000. Additive cubes and a two-dimensional alphabet analogue can be avoided; one-dimensional squares remain open.
why: Separates arithmetic repetition from exact and anagram repetition.
key_works: Vukusic (2025), [*A Lebesgue variant of the additive square problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21200).

title: Mäkelä’s ternary abelian-square conjecture
open: Construct an infinite ternary word whose only abelian-square factors are \(00,11,22\), or prove impossibility.
status: Open for decades. Avoidance of all sufficiently long abelian squares is known, but this sharp restriction is not.
why: Determines an exact alphabet-versus-repetition boundary.
key_works: Fici–Puzynina (2023), [*Abelian Combinatorics on Words: a Survey*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.09937), Conjecture 20.

title: Additive cubes on \(\{0,1,2,3\}\)
open: Does an infinite word on \(\{0,1,2,3\}\) avoid three consecutive equal-length blocks with equal sums?
status: Explicitly open in 2025; other four-element integer alphabets outside the arithmetic-progression equivalence class admit constructions.
why: Completes a precise four-letter alphabet classification.
key_works: Andrade–Mol (2025), [*Avoiding abelian and additive powers in rich words*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15390).

title: Kolakoski density
open: Prove that the self-run-length sequence \(122112122\ldots\) has limiting frequency \(1/2\) for the symbol 1.
status: Oldenburger, 1939; Kolakoski, 1965. Even existence of the limit is unproved; liminf and limsup are tightly constrained.
why: Tests statistical regularity of a simple self-referential process.
key_works: Chvátal (1993/1994), [*Notes on the Kolakoski Sequence*](https://archive.dimacs.rutgers.edu/TechnicalReports/abstracts/1993/93-84.html).

title: Long even Barker sequences
open: Does a binary sequence of even length greater than four have every nonzero-shift aperiodic autocorrelation in \(\{-1,0,1\}\)?
status: Barker, 1953. Odd lengths beyond thirteen are excluded; severe restrictions leave the even case open.
why: Determines whether ideal binary pulse-compression sequences can be longer.
key_works: Willms (2021), [*A note on Barker sequences of even length*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.00502).

title: Asymptotic binary merit factor
open: Determine \(\limsup_n\max_a n^2/(2\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}C_k(a)^2)\) for binary sequences and their aperiodic correlations \(C_k\).
status: Littlewood–Golay problem, developed since the 1960s. Constructions reach approximately 6.34206; even finiteness of the optimum remains open.
why: Sets the ultimate aggregate sidelobe suppression of long binary signals.
key_works: Jedwab–Katz–Schmidt (2013), [*Littlewood Polynomials with Small \(L^4\) Norm*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0260).

title: Eventual periodicity of finite octal games
open: Does every impartial take-and-break game specified by a finite octal code have an eventually periodic Sprague–Grundy sequence?
status: A longstanding Guy problem; many individual codes have certified periods, but the universal statement remains open.
why: Would reduce infinitely many heap positions to finite strategy tables.
key_works: Dailly–Duchêne–Larsson–Paris (2020), [*Partition games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02621); Guy–Nowakowski, [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf) (edition year verify).

title: Infinite three-dimensional Chomp
open: Determine the winner from \(\mathbb N_0^3\), with poisoned origin and moves deleting a chosen point and every coordinatewise larger point.
status: Gale’s question remains unresolved; finite-board strategy stealing does not decide this infinite position.
why: Tests strategy extraction from well-founded infinite position structure.
key_works: Gale (1974), *A curious Nim-type game*; Guy–Nowakowski, [open game problems](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), D1.
prize: Historical Gale offer: US$300; current administration unverified.

title: Exact logical strength of Hindman’s theorem
open: Determine the reverse-mathematical strength of Hindman’s finite-sums theorem over \(\mathsf{RCA}_0\), particularly whether \(\mathsf{ACA}_0\) proves it.
status: Blass–Hirst–Simpson placed it between \(\mathsf{ACA}_0\) and \(\mathsf{ACA}_0^+\) in 1987; the gap remains.
why: Identifies the infinitary resources required by a fundamental theorem.
key_works: Blass–Hirst–Simpson (1987), *Logical analysis of some theorems of combinatorics and topological dynamics*; Carlucci et al. (2020), [restricted Hindman principles](https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.06095).

title: Positive combinatorial rule for Kronecker coefficients
open: Give a uniform positive counting rule for every symmetric-group Kronecker coefficient \(g_{\lambda\mu\nu}\), using explicitly defined finite combinatorial objects.
status: Open for decades. Special families have rules; recent two-row and rectangular results do not cover arbitrary partitions.
why: Would explain tensor-product multiplicities without cancellation.
key_works: Pak–Panova–Swanson (2025), [*A combinatorial interpretation for certain plethysm and Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02312).

title: Positive combinatorial rule for plethysm
open: Give a general positive combinatorial formula for Schur coefficients of \(s_\lambda[s_\mu]\).
status: A longstanding problem; available rules cover restricted outer, inner, or target partitions.
why: Would make composed representation multiplicities structurally understandable.
key_works: Pak–Panova–Swanson (2025), [*A combinatorial interpretation for certain plethysm and Kronecker coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02312).

title: Stanley’s Jack Littlewood–Richardson positivity
open: Prove \(\langle J_\mu^{(\alpha)}J_\nu^{(\alpha)},J_\lambda^{(\alpha)}\rangle_\alpha\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}[\alpha]\), using integral Jack normalization and \(\langle p_\rho,p_\sigma\rangle_\alpha=\delta_{\rho\sigma}z_\rho\alpha^{\ell(\rho)}\).
status: Proposed in 1989. Special parameters and families are understood; general positivity remains open in the 2026 literature.
why: Would provide positive deformed multiplication and convolution laws.
key_works: Stanley (1989), [*Some combinatorial properties of Jack symmetric functions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0001-8708(89)90015-7); Cuenca–Dołęga, [Jack generating functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13098).

title: Combinatorial Schur expansion of modified Macdonald polynomials
open: Give an explicit positive combinatorial formula for every coefficient \(\widetilde K_{\lambda\mu}(q,t)\) in \(\widetilde H_\mu\)’s Schur expansion.
status: Haiman proved positivity geometrically in 2001; a general positive combinatorial rule is still missing.
why: Would explain two-parameter multiplicities through discrete objects.
key_works: Haiman (2001), *Hilbert schemes, polygraphs and the Macdonald positivity conjecture*; Assaf (2018), [*Toward the Schur Expansion of Macdonald Polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.37236/7419).

title: Exact type-\(B\) diagonal-coinvariant dimensions
open: Determine the dimension and bigraded character of \(\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n]/\langle\mathbb C[x,y]^{B_n}_+\rangle\).
status: Studied since the 1990s. The familiar \((2n+1)^n\) lower bound is not exact generally; improved lower bounds lack matching formulas.
why: Tests how type-\(A\) phenomena extend to other reflection groups.
key_works: Ajila–Griffeth (2024), [*Representation theory and the diagonal coinvariant ring of the type B Weyl group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03077).

title: General positive Schubert multiplication rule
open: Give a uniform positive counting rule for all complete-flag Schubert structure constants \(c_{uv}^w\).
status: Open for decades despite geometric nonnegativity; many special descent and permutation classes have rules.
why: Would calculate intersection multiplicities using explicit discrete objects.
key_works: Gao–Zhu (2024/2025), [*Boolean Schubert Structure Coefficients*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05527); Pak–Robichaux (2025), [signed interpretations](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.413).

title: BBDVW recurrence for arbitrary Bruhat intervals
open: Prove the hypercube-decomposition recurrence for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of all symmetric-group Bruhat intervals.
status: Introduced in 2021. Lower intervals \([e,v]\) are settled; arbitrary lower endpoints remain open.
why: Offers a concrete recursive route toward combinatorial invariance.
key_works: Barkley–Gaetz (2026), [*The BBDVW Conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig Polynomials of Lower Intervals*](https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnag022).

title: Exact enumeration of \(1324\)-avoiders
open: Determine a usable exact generating function or structural recurrence for all \(1324\)-avoiding permutations.
status: The outstanding length-four single-pattern enumeration problem. Recent inversion-refined formulas cover only part of the parameter range.
why: Tests the limits of permutation-class decomposition.
key_works: Linusson–Verkama (2025), [*Enumerating 1324-Avoiders with Few Inversions*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: \(1324\) Stanley–Wilf limit
open: Determine \(L(1324)=\lim_n|\operatorname{Av}_n(1324)|^{1/n}\).
status: Existence is proved; the verified interval reported in 2025 is \(10.271<L(1324)<13.5\).
why: Gives a concrete unresolved entropy constant.
key_works: Bevan (2015), [*Permutations avoiding 1324 and patterns in Łukasiewicz paths*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2890); Linusson–Verkama (2025), [inversion-refined enumeration](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: Inversion-refined monotonicity for \(1324\)-avoiders
open: Prove \(\operatorname{av}_n^k(1324)\le\operatorname{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)\) for every \(n,k\).
status: Proposed in 2012; verified in the region \(n\ge(k+7)/2\). General validity would improve the growth upper bound to approximately 13.002.
why: Turns refined monotonicity into a global enumeration improvement.
key_works: Claesson–Jelínek–Steingrímsson (2012), *Upper bounds for the Stanley–Wilf limit of 1324 and other layered patterns*; Linusson–Verkama (2025), [recent progress](https://doi.org/10.37236/13387).

title: Rank-unimodality of permutation-pattern intervals
open: Prove that rank sizes in every finite interval of the classical permutation-pattern poset form a unimodal sequence.
status: McNamara–Steingrímsson, 2015. The consecutive-pattern analogue is known; ordinary containment remains unresolved.
why: Would reveal regularity despite complicated interval topology.
key_works: McNamara–Steingrímsson (2015), [*On the topology of the permutation pattern poset*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2015.02.009).

title: Two unrestricted stacks in series
open: Determine the generating function or asymptotic enumeration of permutations sortable by some sequence of operations through two stacks in series.
status: Studied since Tarjan’s 1972 work. This differs from the solved enumeration for two iterations of West’s deterministic stack-sorting map.
why: Measures the power of a minimal compositional storage model.
key_works: Tarjan (1972), *Sorting Using Networks of Queues and Stacks*; [*Permutations sortable by two stacks in series*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.08663).

title: Real-rooted Durfee polynomials
open: Prove \(D_n(z)=\sum_d p(n,d)z^d\) has only real roots, where \(p(n,d)\) counts partitions of \(n\) with Durfee-square side \(d\).
status: Conjectured in 1998. Asymptotic normality and extensive evidence do not establish real-rootedness.
why: Would impose strong regularity on the full Durfee-size distribution.
key_works: Canfield–Corteel–Savage (1998), [*Durfee Polynomials*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1370).

title: Gabow’s serial symmetric exchange conjecture
open: Order two disjoint bases so that swapping paired elements once each exchanges the bases while both remain bases after every step.
status: Posed in 1976. The regular-matroid case is settled; the general statement survives recent counterexamples to stronger exchange properties.
why: Would provide exceptionally short feasible reconfiguration paths.
key_works: Gabow (1976), *Decomposing symmetric exchanges in matroid bases*; Bérczi–Mátravölgyi–Schwarcz (2026), [*Reconfiguration of basis pairs in regular matroids*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2025.10.009).

title: Cyclic orderability of uniformly dense matroids
open: If \(|E|r(X)\ge r(E)|X|\) for all \(X\subseteq E\), cyclically order \(E\) so every \(r(E)\) consecutive elements form a basis.
status: Kajitani–Ueno–Miyano, 1980s. Coprime size/rank, sparse-paving, and further special cases are known.
why: Converts fractional density into sliding-window independence.
key_works: Bérczi–Jánosik–Mátravölgyi (2026), [*Cyclic Ordering of Split Matroids*](https://doi.org/10.37236/13537).

title: Infinite matroid intersection
open: For arbitrary matroids \(M,N\) on possibly infinite \(E\), find common independent \(I=I_M\sqcup I_N\) with \(\operatorname{cl}_M(I_M)\cup\operatorname{cl}_N(I_N)=E\).
status: Nash-Williams, around 1990. Significant special cases and new augmentation tools leave the unrestricted statement open.
why: Extends min–max duality beyond finite cardinality arguments.
key_works: Bowler (2018), [survey](https://matroidunion.org/?p=2374); Joó (2025), [*Hindrance from a wasteful common independent set*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04342).

title: Almost all matroids are sparse paving
open: Prove \(s_n/m_n\to1\), where \(s_n\) counts labelled sparse paving matroids and \(m_n\) all labelled matroids.
status: Formalized in 2011. Only logarithmic equivalence, \(\log s_n/\log m_n\to1\), is established.
why: Would identify the typical finite independence system.
key_works: Pendavingh–van der Pol (2015), [*On the number of matroids compared to the number of sparse paving matroids*](https://research.tue.nl/en/publications/on-the-number-of-matroids-compared-to-the-number-of-sparse-paving-2/).

title: Leading constant in matroid enumeration
open: Determine \(\log_2m_n\) to relative error \(1+o(1)\), especially its coefficient of \(n^{-1}\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\).
status: Knuth’s lower construction and later upper bounds leave the coefficient between one and \(2+o(1)\).
why: Determines the entropy of finite matroids.
key_works: Knuth (1974), *The asymptotic number of geometries*; Bansal–Pendavingh–van der Pol (2013/2015), [*On the number of matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.6270).

title: Hadamard existence conjecture
open: Construct a sign matrix \(H\) of order \(4m\) satisfying \(HH^{\mathsf T}=4mI\), for every positive integer \(m\).
status: Usually dated to Paley, 1933. Extensive infinite constructions and finite databases do not establish every admissible order.
why: Supplies optimal orthogonal signals, designs, and codes.
key_works: Paley (1933), *On orthogonal matrices*; Cati–Pasechnik (2024/2025), [*A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18897).

title: Skew-Hadamard existence
open: Construct a Hadamard matrix of every order \(4m\) satisfying \(H+H^{\mathsf T}=2I\).
status: A longstanding strengthening of ordinary existence; known skew constructions do not cover every admissible order.
why: Connects orthogonal matrices to regular directed incidence structures.
key_works: Cati–Pasechnik (2024/2025), [*A database of constructions of Hadamard matrices*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18897).

title: Circulant Hadamard conjecture
open: Prove that no circulant Hadamard matrix has order greater than four.
status: Ryser, 1960s. Arithmetic and field-descent restrictions exclude enormous ranges without proving universal nonexistence.
why: Would establish a sharp limit on perfectly orthogonal periodic binary signals.
key_works: Leung–Schmidt (2012), [*New restrictions on possible orders of circulant Hadamard matrices*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-011-9493-1); Borwein–Mossinghoff (2013), [*Wieferich pairs and Barker sequences, II*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0045).

title: Ryser’s odd-order transversal conjecture
open: Prove that every odd-order Latin square has a full transversal.
status: Proposed in 1967. Near-transversals and almost-everywhere transversal decompositions do not settle every odd-order square.
why: Would guarantee simultaneous distinctness in rows, columns, and symbols.
key_works: Montgomery (2024), [*Transversals in Latin Squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.19873); Bowtell–Montgomery (2025), [almost-everywhere decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.05438).

title: Alon–Tarsi Latin-square parity conjecture
open: Prove that the signed sum of order-\(n\) Latin squares is nonzero for every even \(n\), equivalently that \([\prod_{ij}x_{ij}](\det X)^n\ne0\).
status: Proposed in 1992. Orders \(p-1\) and \(p+1\), for odd primes \(p\), are established.
why: Supplies powerful algebraic certificates for decomposition existence.
key_works: Alon–Tarsi (1992), *Colorings and orientations of graphs*; Xu (2026), [Weingarten-calculus formulation](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6g574562).

title: Minimum critical sets in Latin squares
open: Prove that the smallest minimal uniquely completable partial Latin square of order \(n\) has \(\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor\) entries.
status: Conjectured from 1979 onward. A positive constant times \(n^2\) lower bound is known, far from \(1/4\).
why: Determines the least information that uniquely specifies a Latin square.
key_works: Hatami–Qian (2016), [*Teaching dimension, VC dimension, and critical sets in Latin squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.00032).

title: Finiteness of biplanes
open: Determine whether only finitely many nontrivial symmetric \(2\)-\((v,k,2)\) designs exist.
status: A longstanding fixed-\(\lambda\) design problem; known examples and symmetry classifications do not give a universal bound.
why: Would distinguish projective-plane abundance from repeated-pair symmetric designs.
key_works: Kaski–Östergård (2008), [*There are exactly five biplanes with \(k=11\)*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcd.20145); Chen et al. (2025/2026), [double Hall graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10903).

title: Existence of \(S(3,5,41)\)
open: Construct 1,066 five-element blocks on 41 points so that every triple occurs exactly once, or prove impossibility.
status: A longstanding admissible parameter gap retained in the 2025–2026 construction table.
why: Fills an early unresolved small Steiner-system case.
key_works: Kiermaier–Krčadinac–Wassermann, [*Steiner 3-designs as extensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23483); [maintained table](https://web.math.pmf.unizg.hr/~krcko/results/steiner3.html).

title: Prime-power order conjecture
open: Prove that every finite projective plane has prime-power order, or construct a counterexample.
status: Open for decades. Order ten is excluded; order twelve remains unresolved despite strong automorphism restrictions.
why: Asks whether finite-field arithmetic controls the existence spectrum.
key_works: Lam (1991), *The search for a finite projective plane of order 10*; Akiyama–Suetake–Tanaka (2023), [order-twelve restrictions](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcd.21869).

title: Uniqueness of prime-order projective planes
open: Prove every plane of prime order \(p\) is isomorphic to \(\mathrm{PG}(2,p)\), or produce a non-Desarguesian example.
status: A longstanding conjecture. Coding-theoretic uniqueness under extra weight-enumerator hypotheses does not settle the unrestricted statement.
why: Would establish rigidity at prime orders.
key_works: Bagchi (2019), [*A coding theoretic approach to the uniqueness conjecture for projective planes of prime order*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-019-00623-y).

title: Linearity of small minimal blocking sets
open: Prove every minimal \(k\)-blocking set in \(\mathrm{PG}(n,q)\) of size below \(3(q^k+1)/2\) is a linear set over a subfield.
status: Cubic-field cases and dimension reductions are established; general prime-power cases remain.
why: Would derive algebraic structure from a small incidence condition.
key_works: Van de Voorde (2010), [higher-dimensional reductions](https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/2917400); Lavrauw–Storme–Van de Voorde (2011), [cubic-field theorem](https://biblio.ugent.be/publication/1261642).

title: Exact binary rate–distance tradeoff
open: Determine \(R_2(\delta)=\limsup_n n^{-1}\log_2 A_2(n,\lceil\delta n\rceil)\).
status: Gilbert–Varshamov lower bounds and linear-programming upper bounds still leave exponential gaps.
why: Establishes the packing capacity of binary Hamming space.
key_works: Coregliano–Jeronimo–Jones–Linial–Loyfer (2026), [*Higher-Order Delsarte Dual LPs: Lifting, Constructions and Completeness*](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2026.44).

title: Extremal binary self-dual code of length 72
open: Construct a doubly even self-dual binary \([72,36,16]\) code, or prove none exists.
status: Sloane, 1973. Known examples reach distance 12; extensive symmetry restrictions do not decide distance 16.
why: Resolves a central finite code parameter with design and lattice consequences.
key_works: Sloane (1973), [*Is there a \((72,36)\), \(d=16\) self-dual code?*](https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.1973.1054975); Hannusch–Major (2025), [small automorphism groups](https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202506.2100).

title: Sharp Erdős distinct-distance bound
open: Prove every \(n\)-point planar set determines \(\Omega(n/\sqrt{\log n})\) distinct distances.
status: Erdős, 1946. Guth–Katz prove \(\Omega(n/\log n)\); lattice constructions give the conjectured upper scale.
why: Would close the remaining logarithmic gap in planar distance diversity.
key_works: Guth–Katz (2015), [*On the Erdős distinct distance problem in the plane*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.4105).

title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
open: Determine the chromatic number of the plane when points one unit apart must have different colors.
status: The current interval is five to seven; de Grey established the lower bound five in 2018.
why: Connects finite coloring obstructions to Euclidean geometry.
key_works: de Grey (2018), [*The chromatic number of the plane is at least 5*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02385).

title: Exact Erdős–Szekeres convex-polygon numbers
open: Prove that \(2^{k-2}+1\) planar points in general position force \(k\) in convex position.
status: Proposed in 1935. Exact cases through \(k=6\) and asymptotic \(2^{k+o(k)}\) bounds are known; \(k\ge7\) remains open.
why: Determines exact unavoidable convex structure.
key_works: Suk (2017), [*On the Erdős–Szekeres convex polygon problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.08657); Holmsen–Mojarrad–Pach–Tardos (2020), [*Two extensions of the Erdős–Szekeres problem*](https://ems.press/journals/jems/articles/17088).

title: Planar \(k\)-set complexity
open: Determine the maximum number of \(k\)-element subsets of an \(n\)-point planar set separable by a line.
status: Decades-old gap. Dey’s upper bound is \(O(nk^{1/3})\); known lower constructions are substantially smaller.
why: Controls levels in arrangements and geometric selection complexity.
key_works: Dey (1998), *Improved bounds on planar k-sets and related problems*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 7](https://topp.openproblem.net/p7).

title: Danzer’s finite-density hitting set
open: Does a set of finite upper density in \(\mathbb R^d\), \(d\ge2\), intersect every convex body of volume one?
status: Open since the 1960s. Dense forests and weaker visibility constructions do not solve Danzer’s condition.
why: Would give a sparse universal geometric sampling set.
key_works: Adiceam (2020), [*Around the Danzer Problem and the Construction of Dense Forests*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06756).

title: Complex illumination conjecture
open: Prove that every unit ball of a complex norm on \(\mathbb C^d\) can be illuminated by at most \(2^{d+1}-1\) directions.
status: Proposed in 2024, published in 2026. Complex zonoid and other special cases are settled.
why: Identifies how complex symmetry changes covering complexity.
key_works: Rotem–Schejter–Slomka (2026), [*The complex Illumination problem*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00493-025-00195-7).

title: Lebesgue’s universal covering constant
open: Determine the minimum area of a convex planar set containing an isometric copy of every diameter-one planar set.
status: Open since 1914. Bounds are approximately 0.832 to 0.8440935944.
why: Determines the smallest universal geometric container.
key_works: Gibbs (2018), [*An Upper Bound for Lebesgue’s Covering Problem*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.10089); Arman et al. (2025), [covering bounds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04023).

title: Shortest opaque barrier for a square
open: Determine the minimum total length of a planar barrier meeting every line that intersects a unit square.
status: A longstanding opacity problem; improved lower bounds still do not match the best barriers.
why: Measures the minimum material needed for omnidirectional obstruction.
key_works: Kiderlen–Pausinger (2025), [*Explicit lower bounds for opaque sets of unit square and unit disc*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08842).

title: Geometric tetrahedral flip connectivity
open: Are the geometric triangulations of every finite point set in \(\mathbb R^3\) connected through valid bistellar flips?
status: Open even for important restricted configurations; higher-dimensional disconnected examples do not settle three dimensions.
why: Determines whether local retriangulation can explore every tetrahedral mesh.
key_works: [The Open Problems Project, problem 28](https://topp.openproblem.net/p28); Wagner–Welzl (2022), [triangulation study](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-022-00436-2).

title: Voronoi diagrams of lines in three dimensions
open: Determine the maximum combinatorial complexity of the Euclidean Voronoi diagram of \(n\) lines in \(\mathbb R^3\).
status: Quadratic lower bounds and essentially cubic upper bounds remain separated; near-quadratic growth is conjectured.
why: Controls basic proximity computation for spatial line structures.
key_works: Sharir (1994), relevant envelope bounds; [The Open Problems Project, problem 3](https://topp.openproblem.net/p3).

title: Polynomial-time sum-of-square-roots comparison
open: Decide the sign of a difference of sums of square roots of binary-encoded integers in polynomial time.
status: Studied since at least the 1980s; exact arithmetic complexity remains unresolved.
why: Removes a foundational bottleneck in exact geometric optimization.
key_works: Burnikel–Fleischer–Mehlhorn–Schirra (2000), separation bounds; [The Open Problems Project, problem 33](https://topp.openproblem.net/p33).

title: Uniform quadratic-time sorting of \(X+Y\)
open: Given two \(n\)-element real sets, sort all \(n^2\) pairwise sums in uniform \(O(n^2)\) time.
status: Fredman’s 1976 comparison-tree bound is quadratic; a uniform algorithm attaining it remains unknown.
why: Separates comparison complexity from executable algorithmic complexity.
key_works: Fredman (1976), *How good is the information theory bound in sorting?*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 41](https://topp.openproblem.net/p41).

title: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture
open: Bound every \(d\)-polytope’s graph diameter by a polynomial in its number of facets, uniformly in dimension.
status: The original linear Hirsch conjecture is false; general polynomial diameter remains unproved.
why: Would constrain the combinatorial difficulty of navigating linear programs.
key_works: Kalai–Kleitman (1992), *A quasi-polynomial bound for the diameter of graphs of polyhedra*; Santos (2012), [*A counterexample to the Hirsch conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2814).

title: Oda’s integer-decomposition conjecture
open: Prove every smooth lattice polytope \(P\) has the integer-decomposition property: every lattice point of \(kP\) is a sum of \(k\) lattice points of \(P\).
status: Posed in 1997. Numerous classes and low-dimensional cases are known.
why: Connects local smoothness to global integral decomposability.
key_works: Hofscheier–Kasprzyk (2025), [*Is there a smooth lattice polytope which does not have the integer decomposition property?*](https://doi.org/10.14760/SNAP-2025-008-EN).

title: Koszulness of smooth lattice polytopes
open: Prove that the lattice-point semigroup algebra of every smooth lattice polytope is Koszul.
status: Bøgvad’s longstanding conjecture; extensive special-family results leave the general case open.
why: Would tightly control syzygies of smooth toric embeddings.
key_works: Beck–Delgado–Gubeladze–Michałek (2015), [*Very ample and Koszul segmental fibrations*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7422).

title: Unimodular triangulations of smooth polytopes
open: Does every smooth lattice polytope admit a unimodular triangulation?
status: Known for many classes; general dilation theorems do not supply a triangulation of the original polytope.
why: Would give exact lattice decompositions and squarefree algebraic degenerations.
key_works: Haase–Paffenholz–Piechnik–Santos (2021), [*Existence of unimodular triangulations—positive results*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.1687).

title: Gal’s gamma-nonnegativity conjecture
open: Prove the gamma-vector is nonnegative for every flag homology sphere.
status: Proposed in 2005 after stronger real-rootedness failed; many low-dimensional and structured cases are settled.
why: Would reveal hidden positivity in face enumeration.
key_works: Gal (2005), [*Real Root Conjecture fails for five and higher dimensional spheres*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501046).

title: Charney–Davis conjecture
open: For every flag homology \((2d-1)\)-sphere, prove \((-1)^d h(-1)\ge0\).
status: Proposed in 1995. Low-dimensional cases are known; higher-dimensional generality remains open.
why: Connects face enumeration to curvature and Euler-characteristic signs.
key_works: Charney–Davis (1995), [*The Euler characteristic of a nonpositively curved, piecewise Euclidean manifold*](https://people.math.osu.edu/davis.12/old_papers/euler95.pdf).

title: Nevo–Petersen realization of gamma-vectors
open: Realize gamma-vectors of flag homology spheres as face vectors of simplicial complexes, ideally balanced complexes.
status: Proposed in the late 2000s. Barycentric subdivisions and other classes are established.
why: Would turn gamma-positivity into an explicit combinatorial realization.
key_works: Nevo–Petersen (2011), [*On gamma-vectors satisfying the Kruskal–Katona inequalities*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0694); [balanced realizations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.2544).

title: Beck–Fiala in the remaining sparse regime
open: Prove discrepancy \(O(\sqrt t)\) for every set system in which each element belongs to at most \(t\) sets.
status: Proposed in 1981. Recent work resolves \(t\ge\log^2 n\); the full sparse regime remains open.
why: Would make discrepancy depend optimally on column sparsity.
key_works: Bansal–Jiang (2025/2026), [*Decoupling via Affine Spectral-Independence: Beck–Fiala and Komlós Bounds Beyond Banaszczyk*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03961).

title: Strongly polynomial linear programming
open: Solve arbitrary rational linear programs with an operation count polynomial in dimensions and constraints, independent of coefficient bit lengths.
status: Open for decades; weakly polynomial algorithms do not meet this requirement.
why: Would resolve a central complexity question in optimization.
key_works: Smale (1998), *Mathematical problems for the next century*; [The Open Problems Project, problem 8](https://topp.openproblem.net/p8).

title: FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs
open: Approximately count perfect matchings in arbitrary nonbipartite graphs in randomized polynomial time.
status: Bipartite graphs are settled; direct extensions can mix torpidly, while restricted nonbipartite cases are known.
why: Would extend efficient approximation to general dimer systems.
key_works: Štefankovič–Vigoda–Wilmes (2017), [*On Counting Perfect Matchings in General Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07504).

title: Four-thirds subtour-LP conjecture
open: Prove the metric symmetric-TSP subtour relaxation has integrality gap at most \(4/3\).
status: Lower examples approach \(4/3\); the best general upper bound is below \(3/2\) but remains larger.
why: Would expose the exact strength of the standard TSP relaxation.
key_works: Karlin–Klein–Oveis Gharan (2021), [*A (Slightly) Improved Bound on the Integrality Gap of the Subtour LP for TSP*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10043).

title: Constant additive gap for bin packing
open: Bound the integral optimum minus the configuration-LP optimum by an absolute constant.
status: The known general additive bound is \(O(\log\mathrm{OPT})\); constant loss remains open.
why: Would nearly eliminate rounding waste in packing and cutting stock.
key_works: Hoberg–Rothvoss (2017), [*A Logarithmic Additive Integrality Gap for Bin Packing*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.08796).

title: Zigzag fluctuations of random-graph chromatic number
open: Determine the fluctuation scale and limiting distributions of \(\chi(G(n,1/2))\) across all \(n\), including the predicted oscillating scale.
status: Large fluctuations along subsequences are proved; a complete all-\(n\) law is missing.
why: Describes the irregular uncertainty of a basic random optimization parameter.
key_works: Heckel–Riordan (2021/2023), [*How does the chromatic number of a random graph vary?*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14014).

title: Rapid mixing of colorings at \(q\ge\Delta+2\)
open: Prove polynomial mixing of single-site Glauber dynamics for proper \(q\)-colorings of arbitrary maximum-degree-\(\Delta\) graphs whenever \(q\ge\Delta+2\).
status: Decades of progress lower sufficient color counts; general results remain around \(1.809\Delta\), above the conjectured threshold.
why: Would enable efficient sampling close to minimal color availability.
key_works: Carlson–Vigoda (2024), [*Flip Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Improving \((11/6-\varepsilon)\) Using a Simple Metric*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.04870).

title: Planar SAW counting exponent \(43/32\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that planar self-avoiding-walk counts have exponent \(\gamma=43/32\), in \(c_n=\mu^n n^{\gamma-1+o(1)}\).
status: Predicted by Nienhuis in 1982; rigorous exponential growth does not determine this polynomial correction.
why: Would validate a central two-dimensional universality prediction.
key_works: Nienhuis (1982), *Exact critical point and critical exponents of O(n) models in two dimensions*; Grimmett–Li, [*Self-avoiding walks and connective constants*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.05884).

title: Planar SAW displacement exponent \(3/4\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that the characteristic displacement of an \(n\)-step planar self-avoiding walk scales as \(n^{3/4+o(1)}\).
status: The exponent is strongly supported by physics and computation. Sub-ballisticity is rigorous but much weaker.
why: Determines universal polymer swelling.
key_works: Duminil-Copin–Hammond (2013), [*Self-avoiding walk is sub-ballistic*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0401).

title: SAW convergence to \(\mathrm{SLE}_{8/3}\)
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove convergence of suitably rescaled planar lattice self-avoiding walks to \(\mathrm{SLE}_{8/3}\).
status: Predicted in the early 2000s; extensive numerical agreement does not establish the scaling limit.
why: Would connect discrete polymer geometry to conformal probability.
key_works: Lawler–Schramm–Werner (2004), relevant SLE characterization; Kennedy (2002), [*Monte Carlo Tests of SLE Predictions for the 2D Self-Avoiding Walk*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0112246).

title: Four-dimensional strict-SAW logarithmic corrections
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove the predicted logarithmic corrections, including the \(1/4\) exponent, for strict self-avoiding walk on \(\mathbb Z^4\).
status: Rigorous weakly self-avoiding results do not settle the strict model; simulations support the prediction.
why: Resolves behavior at the upper critical dimension.
key_works: Bauerschmidt–Brydges–Slade (2014), weak-model analysis; Fang–Deng–Zhou (2021), [four-dimensional numerical study](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevE.104.064108).

title: Conformal invariance of square-lattice bond percolation
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that critical square-lattice bond-percolation interfaces converge to \(\mathrm{SLE}_6\).
status: The triangular-site model is settled; the square-bond universality transfer remains open.
why: Would establish lattice-independent critical geometry.
key_works: Duminil-Copin (2018), [*Sixty years of percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.04651).

title: Strict convexity of the first-passage limit shape
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove strict convexity and differentiability of the limit shape for ordinary planar first-passage percolation, for example with independent exponential edge weights.
status: The shape theorem is classical; global curvature properties remain unresolved.
why: Would control directional passage times and geodesic geometry.
key_works: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson (2017), [*50 years of first passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03262).

title: KPZ exponents for ordinary first-passage percolation
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove the predicted passage-time fluctuation exponent \(1/3\) and geodesic wandering exponent \(2/3\) for standard planar FPP.
status: Solvable last-passage models exhibit these exponents; ordinary FPP remains unresolved.
why: Tests KPZ universality outside integrable models.
key_works: Auffinger–Damron–Hanson, [*50 years of first passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.03262); [recent primary discussion](https://doi.org/10.1093/imrn/rnae168).

title: Absence of planar FPP bigeodesics
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove almost surely that planar FPP with a standard continuous independent weight law has no doubly infinite geodesic.
status: Directional and conditional nonexistence results are known; unrestricted all-direction nonexistence remains open.
why: Would classify the global structure of optimal paths.
key_works: Damron–Hanson (2017), [*Bigeodesics in first-passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.00804).

title: BKS midpoint problem in dimension three
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Prove that the probability the origin lies on the geodesic between \(-ne_1\) and \(ne_1\) tends to zero in standard FPP on \(\mathbb Z^3\).
status: The planar problem has quantitative solutions; dimensions at least three remain unresolved.
why: Measures delocalization of long optimal paths.
key_works: Dembin–Elboim–Peled (2022), [*Coalescence of geodesics and the BKS midpoint problem in planar first-passage percolation*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02332).

title: Exact square-lattice hard-core critical activity
subfield: Lattice paths, growth models, and statistical mechanics
open: Determine the uniqueness-to-nonuniqueness transition activity \(\lambda_c\) for the hard-core model on \(\mathbb Z^2\).
status: Rigorous upper and lower thresholds remain separated; the numerical prediction is approximately 3.796.
why: Establishes a basic nonintegrable lattice-gas critical point.
key_works: Vera–Vigoda–Yang (2013), [*Improved Bounds on the Phase Transition for the Hard-Core Model in 2-Dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0431).

title: Golomb–Welch perfect Lee-code conjecture
open: For every dimension \(n\ge3\) and integer radius \(r\ge2\), prove that \(\mathbb Z^n\) cannot be partitioned into translates of the Lee ball \(\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:\sum_i|x_i|\le r\}\).
status: Open since 1968. Several low-dimensional and large-radius cases are settled. Leung–Zhou exclude lattice tilings by radius-two Lee balls in every dimension at least three; arbitrary translational tilings need not be lattice tilings.
why: Determines where perfect error correction in the Manhattan metric becomes impossible.
key_works: Peter Horak and Dongryul Kim (2018), [*50 Years of the Golomb–Welch Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03589); Ka Hin Leung and Yue Zhou (2020), [*No lattice tiling of \(\mathbb Z^n\) by Lee sphere of radius 2*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2019.105157).

title: Binary adversarial-deletion zero-rate threshold
open: Determine the supremum \(\delta_*\) of deletion fractions for which binary codes of positive asymptotic rate can uniquely correct every pattern of \(\lfloor\delta n\rfloor\) deletions.
status: Constructions approach \(\sqrt2-1\approx0.4142\). Guruswami–He–Li prove that \(\delta_*<1/2\) by an absolute amount, disproving the former conjectural threshold \(1/2\). The exact threshold remains open.
why: Determines the maximum resilience of positive-rate binary communication against adversarial loss of synchronization.
key_works: Boris Bukh, Venkatesan Guruswami and Johan Håstad (2017), [*An improved bound on the fraction of correctable deletions*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2015/117/); Venkatesan Guruswami, Xiaoyu He and Ray Li (2021), [*The zero-rate threshold for adversarial bit-deletions is less than \(1/2\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.05250).

title: Maximum nonlinearity of a nine-variable Boolean function
open: Determine \(\max_f\min_{\ell\text{ affine}}d_H(f,\ell)\) for \(f:\mathbb F_2^9\to\mathbb F_2\). Equivalently, determine the covering radius of the first-order Reed–Muller code \(RM(1,9)\).
status: Kavut–Yücel constructed functions of nonlinearity \(242\) in 2008; the upper bound is \(244\). A function attaining \(243\) or \(244\), or an impossibility proof closing the gap, remains unknown.
why: Determines the strongest possible resistance to affine approximation at a small but computationally challenging truth-table size.
key_works: Selçuk Kavut and Melek D. Yücel (2008/2010), [*9-variable Boolean Functions with Nonlinearity 242 in the Generalized Rotation Class*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0684); Claude Carlet (2021), *Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Coding Theory*.
aliases: Covering radius of the first-order Reed–Muller code of length \(512\).

title: Complete census of quadratic APN functions in dimension eight
open: Enumerate every CCZ-equivalence class of quadratic APN maps \(\mathbb F_2^8\to\mathbb F_2^8\), with canonical representatives and a checkable completeness certificate. CCZ equivalence means that an invertible affine map of \(\mathbb F_2^{16}\) sends one function’s graph onto the other’s.
status: A 2025 construction supplies \(3{,}775{,}599\) inequivalent examples and estimates roughly six million classes. The catalogue and estimate do not constitute a complete classification.
why: Would provide an exhaustive small-dimensional search space for nonlinear functions, associated codes, and exceptional cryptographic constructions.
key_works: Christof Beierle, Philippe Langevin, Gregor Leander, Alexandr Polujan and Shahram Rasoolzadeh (2025), [*Millions of inequivalent quadratic APN functions in eight variables*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04644).

title: Curling-number termination conjecture
open: For a nonempty finite integer sequence \(S\), let \(k(S)\) be the largest \(k\) for which \(S=XY^k\) with \(Y\ne\varnothing\). Repeatedly append \(k(S)\); prove that a \(1\) eventually appears, whatever the starting sequence.
status: Formulated in the 2000s. Even starts consisting only of \(2\) and \(3\) remain unresolved. Published exhaustive searches cover initial lengths through \(48\); some longer computational conclusions rely on conjectural reductions.
why: Would establish universal termination for a simple string rule whose dependence on its entire history makes conventional induction difficult.
key_works: Benjamin Chaffin and N. J. A. Sloane (2009), [*Curling Numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.2382); Benjamin Chaffin, J. P. Linderman, N. J. A. Sloane and A. R. Wilks (2013), [*On Curling Numbers of Integer Sequences*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.6102).

title: Recurrence of the Kolakoski sequence
open: Does every finite factor of the self-run-length-encoding sequence \(122112122\ldots\) occur infinitely often?
status: The sequence appears in Oldenburger’s 1939 work and Kolakoski’s 1965 rediscovery. Nonperiodicity is known; recurrence remains open and would imply reversal invariance.
why: Determines whether every pattern that appears once must persist throughout the infinite word.
key_works: Alessandro Della Corte (2020), [*Kolakoski Sequence: Links between Recurrence, Symmetry and Limit Density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08306).

title: Complement symmetry of the Kolakoski language
open: Whenever a finite word \(w\) occurs in the Kolakoski sequence, must the word obtained by exchanging every \(1\) and \(2\) also occur?
status: Open despite extensive finite evidence. Complement symmetry implies recurrence; it is a separate assertion from reversal symmetry or equality of digit densities.
why: Would establish a global symmetry that is not apparent from the sequence’s asymmetric initial condition.
key_works: F. Michel Dekking (1997), *What is the Long Range Order in the Kolakoski Sequence?*; Alessandro Della Corte (2020), [*Kolakoski Sequence: Links between Recurrence, Symmetry and Limit Density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08306).

title: Irreducible unimodular Pisot substitution conjecture
open: Prove that the dynamical system of every primitive substitution whose incidence matrix has irreducible characteristic polynomial, determinant \(\pm1\), and Pisot Perron eigenvalue has pure discrete spectrum.
status: A longstanding conjecture from the 1980s. Many classes are settled, including Pisot \(\beta\)-substitutions; arbitrary irreducible unimodular Pisot substitutions remain outside those results.
why: Would connect an algebraic property of a finite substitution rule to quasiperiodic spectral order.
key_works: Marcy Barge (2015), [*The Pisot Conjecture for \(\beta\)-substitutions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.04408); Valérie Berthé and Michel Rigo, editors (2016), *Combinatorics, Words and Symbolic Dynamics*.

title: Eventual periodicity of Grundy’s unequal-splitting game
status: Open since the classical development of impartial games. Flammenkamp reports computations through heap size \(284{,}944{,}236{,}543\), without an established eventual period; observed sparse-value behavior gives conditional approaches.
why: Tests whether a very elementary splitting rule can produce permanently nonperiodic game values.
key_works: Patrick M. Grundy (1939), *Mathematics and games*; Achim Flammenkamp, [*Grundy’s Game*](https://wwwhomes.uni-bielefeld.de/achim/grundy.html), computational tables and commentary.

title: Complete misère analysis of Dawson’s chess
open: Describe the full misère quotient \((Q,P)\) of Dawson’s chess: its monoid operation, losing subset \(P\), and heap-class map \(\Phi(n)\) for arbitrary \(n\). These data should uniformly determine outcomes and winning moves in finite sums.
status: Open since Dawson’s 1935 formulation. For the equivalent heap game \(0.07\), the quotient restricted to heaps of size at most \(33\) has \(638\) elements; a full description remains unknown.
why: Would extend practical misère algebra to one of its oldest major test cases.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2008), [*Misère quotients for impartial games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609825); Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), problem A15.
prize: US$500 offered by Plambeck, reported in the 2025 survey; present administration has not been independently confirmed.

title: The wild quaternary game \(0.3102\)
open: Describe the full misère quotient, its losing classes, and the heap-class map for the game with these moves: remove one token freely; remove two only when doing so empties the heap; or remove four while leaving a nonempty heap.
status: Retained in the 2025 problem list. The partial quotient through heap size \(11\) has \(74\) elements; no complete quotient description is known.
why: Exhibits difficult misère behavior without even allowing heaps to split.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2008), [*Misère quotients for impartial games*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609825), Appendix A.4; Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf), A15.
prize: US$200 offered by Plambeck, reported in the 2025 survey; present administration has not been independently confirmed.

title: Recognizing infinite misère quotients
open: Given a finite, explicitly represented collection of finite impartial games, decide whether the misère quotient of its closure under followers and disjunctive sums is infinite. Establish a general decision algorithm or prove undecidability.
status: Listed by Plambeck–Siegel and retained in Nowakowski’s 2025 survey. Existing quotient algorithms handle many finite cases but provide no general termination guarantee when the quotient is infinite.
why: Would establish whether a major failure mode of automated game analysis can be recognized algorithmically.
key_works: Thane E. Plambeck and Aaron N. Siegel (2007), [*Misère quotients for impartial games: Supplementary material*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.2404); Richard J. Nowakowski (2025), [*Unsolved problems in combinatorial games*](https://library.slmath.org/books/Book71/files/GONC6-04.pdf).

title: Symmetric Mahler volume-product conjecture
open: For every origin-symmetric convex body \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\), prove
status: Originates in Mahler’s 1930s work. Iriyeh–Shibata prove the three-dimensional symmetric case, including equality. Unconditional bodies and other structured classes are known; general reverse Santaló inequalities give the dimensional scale without the sharp constant.
why: Would determine the smallest possible volume product of a norm ball and its dual.
key_works: Hiroshi Iriyeh and Masataka Shibata (2020), [*Symmetric Mahler’s conjecture for the volume product in the three dimensional case*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01749); Jean Bourgain and Vitali Milman (1987), *New volume ratio properties for convex symmetric bodies in \(\mathbb R^n\)*.

title: Ulam’s least-dense-packing conjecture
open: Prove that every three-dimensional convex body admits a packing by congruent copies of density at least \(\pi/\sqrt{18}\), the optimal sphere-packing density. Arbitrary rotations are allowed.
status: Recorded as Ulam’s conjecture in the 1970s. Kallus proves that the ball is a local pessimum among origin-symmetric convex bodies, covering sufficiently small symmetric deformations. Arbitrary convex shapes remain unresolved.
why: Would establish a universal lower packing efficiency for convex particles and identify the sphere as the global worst case.
key_works: Yoav Kallus (2014), [*The 3-ball is a local pessimum for packing*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.2551); Thomas Hales (2005), *A proof of the Kepler conjecture*.

title: Optimal packing density of regular tetrahedra
open: Determine the supremal density of packings of congruent regular tetrahedra in \(\mathbb R^3\), allowing arbitrary rotations and nonperiodic arrangements. In particular, is \(4000/4671\) globally optimal?
status: Chen–Engel–Glotzer construct a dimer crystal of density \(4000/4671\approx0.856347\) in 2010. Rigorous upper bounds remain far from certifying this value; optimization over small periodic cells cannot exclude larger cells or nonperiodic improvements.
why: Would determine a basic packing optimum for nonspherical particles and calibrate computational crystal searches.
key_works: Elizabeth Chen, Michael Engel and Sharon Glotzer (2010), [*Dense crystalline dimer packings of regular tetrahedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0586); Simon Gravel, Veit Elser and Yoav Kallus (2011), [*Upper bound on the packing density of regular tetrahedra and octahedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2830).

title: Voronoi’s parallelohedron conjecture
open: Prove that every convex polytope tiling \(\mathbb R^d\) by translations is affinely equivalent to the Dirichlet–Voronoi cell of a lattice.
status: Posed in 1908. Many structural classes are known. Garber’s proof for all five-dimensional parallelohedra was published in 2025; the universal cases in dimensions at least six remain open.
why: Would classify convex translational tiles through quadratic forms and nearest-lattice-point geometry.
key_works: Alexey Garber (2025), [*Voronoi conjecture for five-dimensional parallelohedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.05193); Alexey Garber, Andrey Gavrilyuk and Alexander Magazinov (2014), [*The Voronoi conjecture for parallelohedra with simply connected \(\delta\)-surface*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.1019).

title: Gilbert–Pollak Steiner-ratio conjecture
open: Prove that for every finite planar point set, the Euclidean Steiner minimum tree has length at least \(\sqrt3/2\) times the Euclidean minimum spanning tree length. Equilateral triangles attain equality.
status: Proposed in 1968. A famous claimed complete proof contains a gap. Ke and collaborators’ published 2026 work reports the certified partial lower bound \(0.8559\), below the conjectured \(0.866025\ldots\).
why: Determines the largest possible saving obtained by introducing additional junctions into a shortest connecting network.
key_works: Edgar Gilbert and Henry Pollak (1968), *Steiner minimal trees*; Yisi Ke, Tianyu Huang, Yankai Shu, Di He, Jingchu Gai and Liwei Wang (2026), [*Towards Solving the Gilbert-Pollak Conjecture via Large Language Models*](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v306/ke26a.html).

title: Unbounded fatness of convex four-polytopes
status: Highlighted by Eppstein–Kuperberg–Ziegler in 2003. Constructions exceed bounds available for simple or simplicial polytopes. Strongly regular cell decompositions of the three-sphere can have unbounded fatness, but convex realizability remains the crucial additional constraint.
why: Would resolve a major qualitative uncertainty about realizable face vectors in dimension four.
key_works: David Eppstein, Greg Kuperberg and Günter Ziegler (2003), [*Fat 4-polytopes and fatter 3-spheres*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0204007); Günter Ziegler (2004), *Face numbers of 4-polytopes and 3-spheres*.

title: Optimal size of planar weak epsilon-nets
open: Determine the smallest worst-case size \(f_2(\epsilon)\) of a set piercing every convex region containing at least an \(\epsilon\) fraction of a given finite planar point set. Piercing points may lie outside the input set.
status: Studied since the early 1990s. Rubin gives \(f_2(\epsilon)=O(\epsilon^{-3/2-\gamma})\) for every fixed \(\gamma>0\). The lower bound \(\Omega(\epsilon^{-1}\log(1/\epsilon))\) leaves an exponent gap.
why: Determines how efficiently all large convex ranges can be represented by a small set of witnesses.
key_works: Natan Rubin (2022), [*An Improved Bound for Weak Epsilon-Nets in the Plane*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.02686); Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch (2011), *Lower bounds for weak epsilon-nets and stair-convexity*.

title: Exact planar Hadwiger–Debrunner \((4,3)\) piercing number
open: Determine the least integer \(h\) such that every finite family of planar convex sets, among every four of which some three intersect, can be pierced by \(h\) points. The conjectured value is three.
status: A concrete case of the 1957 Hadwiger–Debrunner program. The \((p,q)\) theorem establishes finiteness. McGinnis improves the universal upper bound from thirteen to nine; examples require three, leaving \(3\le h\le9\).
why: Would quantify exactly how a local intersection condition restricts a global transversal.
key_works: Daniel McGinnis (2022), [*A family of convex sets in the plane satisfying the \((4,3)\)-property can be pierced by nine points*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13195); András Gyárfás, Daniel Kleitman and Géza Tóth (2001), *Convex sets in the plane with three of every four meeting*.

title: Polynomial-time rotation distance
open: Determine whether the minimum number of rotations transforming one ordered rooted binary tree into another with the same ordered leaves can be computed in polynomial time. Equivalently, compute exact flip distance between triangulations of a convex polygon.
status: Open since the classical 1980s work on rotation distance. Constant-factor approximation and fixed-parameter algorithms in the distance are known; Cleary–St. John obtain a linear-size kernel. General polynomial-time exact computation remains unresolved.
why: Would settle the complexity of a fundamental local reconfiguration metric used in data structures and associahedron geometry.
key_works: Sean Cleary and Katherine St. John (2009), [*Rotation distance is fixed-parameter tractable*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipl.2009.04.023); Anoop S. K. M. and Jayalal Sarma (2023), [*On Rotation Distance of Rank Bounded Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03985).

title: Conway’s thrackle conjecture
open: Prove that a drawing of a finite simple graph in the plane in which every pair of distinct edges meets exactly once—at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing—has at most as many edges as vertices.
status: Posed in the late 1960s. Straight-line thrackles satisfy the conjecture. Xu’s 2021 general improvement gives coefficient \(1.393\) in the corresponding connected bound; unrestricted drawings with curved edges remain unresolved.
why: Tests how strongly an extreme pairwise crossing rule constrains a graph’s global size.
key_works: Radoslav Fulek and János Pach (2017), [*Thrackles: An Improved Upper Bound*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08037); Yian Xu (2021), [*A New Upper Bound for Conway’s Thrackles*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amc.2020.125573).

title: Explicit point sets with optimal linear dimension dependence
open: Construct, in deterministic time polynomial in \(d\) and \(1/\epsilon\), rational point sets \(P\subset[0,1]^d\) of size \(O(d\epsilon^{-2})\) with star discrepancy at most \(\epsilon\), uniformly for \(d\ge1\) and \(0<\epsilon<1\). Star discrepancy measures the largest error over all axis-parallel boxes anchored at the origin.
status: Heinrich–Novak–Wasilkowski–Woźniakowski prove existence in 2001 by probabilistic methods. Dick–Pillichshammer’s 2025/2026 work obtains almost-optimal dimension dependence using randomly shifted lattice constructions. A deterministic polynomial-time construction attaining the stated bound remains open.
why: Would turn optimal high-dimensional integration guarantees into efficiently reproducible deterministic point sets.
key_works: Stefan Heinrich, Erich Novak, Grzegorz Wasilkowski and Henryk Woźniakowski (2001), *The inverse of the star-discrepancy depends linearly on the dimension*; Josef Dick and Friedrich Pillichshammer (2025/2026), [*The star discrepancy of a union of randomly digitally shifted Korobov polynomial lattice point sets depends polynomially on the dimension*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.15877).

title: Whitehead’s asphericity conjecture
open: Must every connected subcomplex of an aspherical two-dimensional CW complex be aspherical? Here aspherical means that all homotopy groups in dimensions at least two vanish.
status: Open since Whitehead’s 1941 work. Diagrammatic methods establish many special classes, including suitable labeled oriented trees. Rational and \(p\)-adic analogues have advanced, but the original integral conjecture remains open.
why: Would explain when deleting cells preserves the absence of higher homotopy, connecting cell combinatorics with group presentations.
key_works: Stephan Rosebrock (2026), [*Labelled Oriented Trees and the Whitehead Conjecture*](https://www.mathematik.uni-mainz.de/en/2026/01/12/mathematics-colloquium-15-1-26-stephan-rosebrock-karlsruhe-labelled-oriented-trees-and-the-whitehead-conjecture/); A. M. Mikhovich (2025), [*Rational and \(p\)-adic analogues of J. H. C. Whitehead’s conjecture*](https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/im9597).

title: Decidability of embedding two-complexes in four-space
open: Given a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex, decide whether it admits a PL embedding into \(\mathbb R^4\), or prove that no such decision algorithm exists.
status: A longstanding exceptional case in algorithmic embedding theory. The problem is NP-hard, and deleted-product obstructions are incomplete. Georgakopoulos–Winter’s 2024 work develops embeddability-preserving operations without settling decidability.
why: Would locate a fundamental limit of finite topological computation in a critical codimension.
key_works: Agelos Georgakopoulos and Martin Winter (2024), [*On 2-complexes embeddable in 4-space, and the excluded minors of their underlying graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12681); Jiří Matoušek, Martin Tancer and Uli Wagner (2011), *Hardness of embedding simplicial complexes in \(\mathbb R^d\)*.

title: FPRAS for unrestricted integer contingency tables
open: Approximate the number of nonnegative integer matrices with specified row and column sums within relative error \(\epsilon\), with high probability, in time polynomial in the binary input length and \(1/\epsilon\). Both dimensions must be allowed to grow.
status: Studied intensively since the 1990s. FPRAS algorithms exist when one dimension is fixed and in sufficiently large-margin regimes. No known method gives the required uniform guarantee for arbitrary margins and unbounded row and column counts.
why: Would support certified counting, sampling, and exact-margin statistical tests without restrictive assumptions on the table.
key_works: Martin Dyer, Ravi Kannan and John Mount (1997), *Sampling contingency tables*; Mary Cryan, Martin Dyer and Dana Randall (2010), [*Approximately Counting Integral Flows and Cell-Bounded Contingency Tables*](https://doi.org/10.1137/060650544).

title: Unique Games conjecture
open: For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), is there an alphabet size for which it is NP-hard to distinguish permutation-constraint instances with optimum at least \(1-\epsilon\) from those with optimum at most \(\epsilon\)?
status: Proposed by Khot in 2002. Subexponential algorithms and major hardness theorems for related 2-to-2 games constrain the possibilities. The corresponding results with imperfect completeness do not establish the required near-perfect-completeness statement for unique constraints.
