why: Would establish sharp approximation barriers for many combinatorial optimization problems from one constraint-satisfaction hypothesis.
key_works: Subhash Khot (2002), [*On the power of unique 2-prover 1-round games*](https://doi.org/10.1145/509907.510017); Subhash Khot, Dor Minzer and Muli Safra (2023), [*Pseudorandom sets in Grassmann graph have near-perfect expansion*](https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2023.198.1.1).

title: Log-rank conjecture
open: For every nonzero finite Boolean communication matrix \(M\), is its deterministic communication complexity bounded by a fixed polynomial in \(1+\log\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}(M)\), with universal constants independent of the matrix dimensions?
status: Formulated by Lovász–Saks in 1988. Sudakov–Tomon improve the general upper bound to \(O(\sqrt{\operatorname{rank}M})\) in work published in 2025. Hambardzumyan–Lovett–Shirley’s February 2026 revision gives new equivalent formulations, leaving the polylogarithmic target open.
why: Would connect linear-algebraic simplicity with efficient two-party communication.
key_works: Benny Sudakov and István Tomon (2025), [*Matrix discrepancy and the log-rank conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.18524); Lianna Hambardzumyan, Shachar Lovett and Morgan Shirley (2026), [*The Log-Rank Conjecture: New Equivalent Formulations*](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2025/141/).

title: Toeplitz’s square-peg problem for arbitrary Jordan curves
open: Does every continuous simple closed curve in the plane contain four distinct points forming a square? No smoothness, rectifiability, or finite-length assumption may be imposed.
status: Posed in 1911. Smooth curves and many other regularity classes are settled. Greene–Lobb’s 2026 paper establishes new Lipschitz two-graph cases. Approximation by smooth curves can produce squares collapsing to a point, leaving the arbitrary continuous case open.
why: Tests whether topology alone forces a universal finite geometric pattern.
key_works: Joshua Evan Greene and Andrew Lobb (2021), *The rectangular peg problem*; Greene and Lobb (2026), [*Square pegs between two graphs*](https://doi.org/10.4171/CMH/619), [arXiv:2407.07798](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07798).

title: Sharp three-dimensional first-selection constant
open: Determine the largest \(c_3\) such that every \(n\)-point set in general position in \(\mathbb R^3\) has a point lying in at least \((c_3-o(1))\binom n4\) of its spanned tetrahedra. The conjectured value is \(3/32\).
status: Studied since the 1980s. Clustered constructions give the upper bound \(3/32\) in this normalization. Gromov’s method and Matoušek–Wagner’s refinements improve positive lower bounds without reaching that value.
why: Would determine the strongest universal simplicial-depth guarantee for three-dimensional point clouds.
key_works: Boris Bukh, Jiří Matoušek and Gabriel Nivasch (2010), *Stabbing simplices by points and flats*; Jiří Matoušek and Uli Wagner (2014), [*On Gromov’s method of selecting heavily covered points*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.3515).

title: Efficient refutation of sparse random 3-SAT
open: For some sufficiently large fixed \(c\), construct a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies unsatisfiability with high probability for a uniformly random 3-CNF with \(n\) variables and \(cn\) clauses, while never certifying a satisfiable formula. Alternatively, prove a computational obstruction under a clearly stated assumption.
status: A central average-case complexity problem since the 1980s–2000s. Feige–Ofek give polynomial-time refutation at order \(n^{3/2}\) clauses. The existence of shorter certificates in sparser regimes does not imply efficient discovery of certificates at constant density.
why: Separates efficiently recognizing typical unsatisfiability from proving that random formulas are almost surely unsatisfiable.
key_works: Uriel Feige and Eran Ofek (2007), [*Easily refutable subformulas of large random 3CNF formulas*](https://doi.org/10.4086/toc.2007.v003a002); Sarah Allen, Ryan O’Donnell and David Witmer (2015), [*How to refute a random CSP*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/random-csp-refutation.pdf).

title: Algorithmic threshold of the symmetric binary perceptron
open: For fixed \(\kappa>0\), determine the largest constraint density \(\alpha\) at which a polynomial-time algorithm can, with high probability, find \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) satisfying \(|Gx|\le\kappa\sqrt n\) coordinatewise, where \(G\) has \(\lfloor\alpha n\rfloor\) independent standard-Gaussian rows.
status: The satisfiability threshold is known, but the efficient-search threshold is not. Gamarnik–Kızıldağ–Perkins–Xu establish a multi-overlap-gap barrier for stable algorithms below the satisfiability threshold. Low-density search algorithms leave the general threshold unresolved.
why: Provides a precise test of how the geometry of a random solution space obstructs training discrete classifiers.
key_works: David Gamarnik, Eren Kızıldağ, Will Perkins and Changji Xu (2022), [*Algorithms and Barriers in the Symmetric Binary Perceptron Model*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15667).

title: Unrestricted uniform sampling for the symmetric binary perceptron
open: At fixed positive density below the satisfiability threshold, can a randomized polynomial-time algorithm output an approximately uniform satisfying assignment of the symmetric binary perceptron, with total-variation error tending to zero? Settle feasibility or establish a suitable complexity-theoretic obstruction.
status: Efficient search succeeds at sufficiently low density. El Alaoui’s 2025 theorem rules out approximate uniform sampling by stable algorithms and bounded-depth Boolean circuits at every positive density; these restrictions do not cover all polynomial-time algorithms.
why: Would determine whether efficiently found solutions can represent a typical feasible configuration.
key_works: Ahmed El Alaoui (2025), [*Hardness of Sampling Solutions From the Symmetric Binary Perceptron*](https://doi.org/10.1002/rsa.70021).

title: Infinite interchange cycles in dimensions three and four
open: Prove that nearest-neighbor random interchange on \(\mathbb Z^3\) and \(\mathbb Z^4\) has infinite permutation cycles with positive probability for all sufficiently large fixed times. Each edge rings independently at rate one and swaps its endpoint labels.
status: Part of Tóth’s 1993 conjecture. Elboim–Sly establish existence in every dimension at least five in their 2022–2024 work. Numerical evidence supports macroscopic cycles in dimension three, but the low-dimensional theorem remains open.
why: Would establish a spatial permutation phase transition in dimensions where repeated encounters defeat current high-dimensional methods.
key_works: Dor Elboim and Allan Sly (2022/2024), [*Infinite cycles in the interchange process in five dimensions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17023); Alessandro Barp et al. (2015), [*A numerical study of the 3D random interchange and random loop models*](https://doi.org/10.1088/1751-8113/48/34/345002).

title: Roughening transition of the three-dimensional Ising interface
open: Prove that the standard nearest-neighbor three-dimensional Ising model has a roughening transition strictly below its bulk critical temperature: its Dobrushin interface is rigid at low temperature but delocalized in a nonempty higher-temperature ordered regime.
status: Predicted for roughly half a century. Low-temperature rigidity is classical. Related solid-on-solid models have rigorous roughening theorems; overhangs and bubbles obstruct transfer to the full Ising interface. A 2026 tensor-network study supplies further numerical evidence.
why: Would rigorously explain how crystal facets disappear while bulk order survives.
key_works: Roland Dobrushin (1972), *Gibbs state describing coexistence of phases for a three-dimensional Ising model*; Atsushi Ueda, Lander Burgelman, Luca Tagliacozzo and Laurens Vanderstraeten (2026), [*Interface roughening in the 3-D Ising model with tensor networks*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.07829).

title: Bounded fluctuations of planar rotor-router aggregation
open: For clockwise rotor-router aggregation on \(\mathbb Z^2\), with all rotors initially aligned and particles launched successively from the origin, is the occupied cluster after \(N\) particles within a bounded radial distance of the disk of area \(N\), uniformly in \(N\)?
status: The Euclidean limit shape is proved, and Levine–Peres establish \(O(\log r)\) fluctuations at radius \(r\). Simulations suggest an \(O(1)\) radial error for standard initial configurations.
why: Would quantify the unusually strong fluctuation suppression produced by a deterministic local rule.
key_works: Lionel Levine and Yuval Peres (2017), [*Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.00411); Levine and Peres (2009), [*Strong Spherical Asymptotics for Rotor-Router Aggregation and the Divisible Sandpile*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11118-008-9104-6).

title: Ferrari–Spohn limit for the top SOS level line above a wall
open: For the low-temperature \((2+1)\)-dimensional solid-on-solid model in an \(L\times L\) square with zero boundary heights and a hard floor, prove a Ferrari–Spohn diffusion limit for the top macroscopic level line near the middle of a side, with horizontal scale \(L^{2/3}\) and vertical scale \(L^{1/3}\). Take subsequences along which the fractional part of \((4\beta)^{-1}\log L\) converges away from a layering-transition value, and identify the limiting diffusion and its parameters.
status: Cube-root fluctuation bounds are known. Caddeo–Kim–Lubetzky prove a matching-order lower bound and the diffusion limit for a related setup with specially chosen boundary heights. The spontaneously selected top loop in the original box remains unresolved.
why: Would identify the complete fluctuation process of a random crystal facet.
key_works: Patrizio Caddeo, Yujin H. Kim and Eyal Lubetzky (2024), [*On level line fluctuations of SOS surfaces above a wall*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09106).

title: Bijective harmonious labeling of every tree
open: For every \(n\)-vertex tree, find a bijection \(f:V(T)\to\mathbb Z_n\) such that its \(n-1\) edge sums \(f(u)+f(v)\) are distinct.
status: Part of the harmonious-labeling program originating in 1980. Müyesser–Pokrovskiy’s 2025 preprint establishes bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees; unrestricted degree patterns remain open.
why: Connects additive permutations with rainbow tree embeddings in algebraically colored complete graphs.
key_works: Graham–Sloane (1980), *On additive bases and harmonious graphs*; Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Graham–Sloane harmonious tree conjecture
open: Label an \(m\)-edge tree’s \(m+1\) vertices by \(\mathbb Z_m\), using every label and repeating exactly one, so that all \(m\) edge sums are distinct modulo \(m\).
status: Proposed in 1980; verified computationally for trees through 31 vertices. Bounded-degree cases for sufficiently large trees are now known. The modulus and permitted repetition distinguish this from the preceding problem.
why: Would realize every cyclic-group element exactly once as an edge sum.
key_works: Fang (2011), [*New Computational Result on Harmonious Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3490); Müyesser–Pokrovskiy (2025), [*On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280).

title: Super edge-magic tree conjecture
open: Label the vertices and edges of every \(n\)-vertex tree bijectively with \(1,\ldots,2n-1\), assigning \(1,\ldots,n\) to vertices, so that \(f(u)+f(uv)+f(v)\) is constant over all edges.
status: Enomoto–Lladó–Nakamigawa–Ringel, 1998. Caterpillars, additional families, and all trees through 17 vertices are established.
why: Tests whether arbitrary tree structure supports simultaneous bijectivity and a rigid additive conservation rule.
key_works: Enomoto et al. (1998), *Super edge-magic graphs*; Ichishima–López–Muntaner-Batle–Takahashi (2022), [*Recent studies on the super edge-magic deficiency of graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.04029).

title: Faudree–Lehel irregularity-strength conjecture
open: Is there an absolute \(C\) such that every \(d\)-regular \(n\)-vertex graph, \(d\ge2\), has edge weights in \(1,\ldots,\lceil n/d\rceil+C\) making all weighted vertex degrees distinct?
status: Open since 1987. Asymptotic bounds approach \(n/d\), and an additive 28 is available in sufficiently dense degree ranges. A uniform additive constant remains missing.
why: Would determine whether the elementary counting obstruction explains essentially the entire labeling cost.
key_works: Faudree–Lehel (1987), *Bound on the irregularity strength of regular graphs*; Przybyło–Wei (2023), [*Short Proof of the Asymptotic Confirmation of the Faudree–Lehel Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.37236/11413).

title: Adjacent-vertex-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: Does every connected graph of order at least three, except \(C_5\), have a proper edge coloring with \(\Delta+2\) colors such that adjacent vertices see different sets of incident colors?
status: Proposed in 2002. Joret–Lochet improve Hatami’s \(\Delta+300\) bound to \(\Delta+19\) for sufficiently large maximum degree; additive two remains open.
why: Measures the extra scheduling information needed to distinguish neighboring vertices.
key_works: Zhang–Liu–Wang (2002), *Adjacent strong edge coloring of graphs*; Joret–Lochet (2020), [*Progress on the Adjacent Vertex Distinguishing Edge Coloring Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.06104).

title: Proper neighbor-sum-distinguishing edge-coloring conjecture
open: For every graph with no isolated edge or \(C_5\) component, properly color its edges with integers \(1,\ldots,\Delta+2\) so that adjacent vertices have different sums of incident colors.
status: Proposed in 2013. The general asymptotic bound is \(\Delta+O(\sqrt\Delta)\). Requiring proper edge colors makes this a surviving problem after the 1–2–3 theorem.
why: Combines conflict-free edge schedules with locally readable numerical identifiers.
key_works: Flandrin–Marczyk–Przybyło–Saclé–Woźniak (2013), *Neighbor sum distinguishing index*; Kalinowski–Pilśniak–Sidorowicz–Turowska (2026), [*Quasi-majority neighbor sum distinguishing edge-colorings*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.01835).

title: The 1–2 total-weighting conjecture
open: Weight every graph’s vertices and edges from \(\{1,2\}\) so that \(w(v)+\sum_{e\ni v}w(e)\) differs across every edge.
status: Przybyło–Woźniak, 2010. Deng–Qiu proved the conjecture for regular graphs in 2025; the unrestricted case remains open.
why: Asks for the smallest alphabet supporting a proper vertex coloring generated entirely by additive local data.
key_works: Przybyło–Woźniak (2010), *On a 1,2 conjecture*; Deng–Qiu (2025), [*The 1–2 conjecture holds for regular graphs*](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0095895625000371).

title: Four locally irregular edge classes
open: If a graph admits any edge partition into locally irregular subgraphs, must four such subgraphs suffice? In each subgraph, adjacent vertices must have different degrees.
status: The three-class conjecture from 2015 is false; four is the revised target following the bow-tie counterexample. General constant upper bounds remain above four.
why: Seeks the correct universal decomposition number after identifying a genuine obstruction to three.
key_works: Sedlar–Škrekovski (2021), [*Remarks on the Local Irregularity Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.08111); Grzelec–Woźniak (2022), [*On decomposing multigraphs into locally irregular submultigraphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.08809).

title: Exact nonrepetitive chromatic number of the square grid
open: Determine the fewest colors for the infinite square grid such that no simple path has a color sequence consisting of two consecutive identical blocks.
status: Graph nonrepetitive coloring dates to around 2000. Tianyi Tao’s work, published in 2026, gives bounds of five and twelve.
why: Tests how one-dimensional repetition avoidance behaves under Cartesian products.
key_works: Alon–Grytczuk–Hałuszczak–Riordan (2002), *Nonrepetitive colorings of graphs*; Tianyi Tao (2026), [*The nonrepetitive coloring of grids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16237).

title: Vizing’s 2-factor conjecture
open: Must every connected edge-chromatic critical graph with chromatic index \(\Delta+1\) contain a spanning 2-regular subgraph? Critical means deleting any edge lowers the chromatic index.
status: Open since the 1960s. Cases with \(\Delta\ge n/2\) are known; additional results combine degree and toughness, including toughness at least \(3/2\) and \(\Delta\ge n/3\).
why: Would force a spanning cycle system inside every minimal obstruction to optimal edge coloring.
key_works: Vizing (1968), *Some unsolved problems in graph theory*; Kanno–Shan (2019), [*Vizing’s 2-Factor Conjecture Involving Toughness and Maximum Degree Conditions*](https://doi.org/10.37236/7353).

title: The \(K_5\) and \(K_6\) cases of Hajós’ subdivision conjecture
open: Must every graph of chromatic number at least \(k\) contain a subdivision of \(K_k\), for \(k=5\) and separately for \(k=6\)?
status: Hajós, 1961. The assertion is true through \(k=4\), false for \(k\ge7\), and unresolved at these two intermediate values.
why: Locates the boundary at which chromatic complexity ceases to force topological cliques.
key_works: Catlin (1979), [*Hajós’ Graph-Coloring Conjecture: Variations and Counterexamples*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(79)90062-5); Hayashi–Kawarabayashi–Yoo (2025), [*Chasing Tripods to Obtain a Rooted Subdivision*](https://doi.org/10.1137/23M157082X).

title: Bouchet’s signed 6-flow conjecture
open: Does every flow-admissible signed graph admit a nowhere-zero integer flow whose edge values have absolute value at most five, with signed incidence conventions governing conservation?
status: Proposed in 1983. An 11-flow theorem holds generally. Nurse’s January 2026 preprint establishes the conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected cubic signed graphs.
why: Extends the nowhere-zero flow program to obstructions introduced by negative edges.
key_works: Bouchet (1983), *Nowhere-zero integral flows on a bidirected graph*; Nurse (2026), [*Bouchet’s conjecture for cyclically 5-edge-connected, cubic signed graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05692).

title: Seymour’s planar multigraph edge-coloring conjecture
open: Is every loopless planar \(r\)-regular multigraph with \(|\delta(S)|\ge r\) for every odd-cardinality vertex set \(S\) properly edge-colorable with \(r\) colors?
status: Proposed in the 1970s. The cubic case is the four-color theorem. Chen–Naserasr’s 2025 preprint establishes further cases through signed bipartite partial 3-trees and planar duality.
why: Would turn the relevant fractional matching conditions into an exact perfect-matching decomposition theorem.
key_works: Chen–Naserasr (2025), [*Bounding signed bipartite partial \(t\)-trees and application to edge-coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14304).

title: Planar circular flow conjecture
open: Does every \(2k\)-edge-connected planar graph admit a circular \((2+2/k)\)-flow, meaning a conservative real flow with edge magnitudes between \(1\) and \(1+2/k\)?
status: Related to Jaeger’s 1980s conjectures. The unrestricted-graph version is false. Known planar results include \(5/2\)-flows at edge connectivity ten and \(7/3\)-flows at connectivity sixteen.
why: Planar duality turns this into sharp circular-coloring guarantees from girth.
key_works: Jaeger (1988), *Nowhere-zero flow problems*; Cranston–Li (2020), [*Circular Flows in Planar Graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.09833).

title: DeVos’ Cayley-homomorphism flow-transfer conjecture
open: If \(\mathrm{Cay}(M,B)\to\mathrm{Cay}(M',B')\) is a graph homomorphism between Cayley graphs of finite abelian groups with symmetric connection sets, must every graph with a \(B\)-valued \(M\)-flow have a \(B'\)-valued \(M'\)-flow?
status: Formulated by DeVos and investigated by Hušek–Šámal in 2020. A stronger proposed transfer statement is false; the original remains open.
why: Would connect homomorphism order with constrained flow existence.
key_works: Hušek–Šámal (2020), [*Homomorphisms of Cayley graphs and Cycle Double Covers*](https://doi.org/10.37236/8456).

title: Three longest paths have a common vertex
open: Must every three longest paths in a connected graph share a vertex?
status: Popularized by Zamfirescu since the 1980s. Every pair intersects, but Gallai’s stronger question about one vertex common to all longest paths is false.
why: Is the first unresolved Helly-type intersection condition after the pairwise case.
key_works: Axenovich (2009), *When do three longest paths have a common vertex?*; Groenland–Longbrake–Steiner–Turcotte–Yepremyan (2025), [*Longest cycles in vertex-transitive and highly connected graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04618), §5.

title: Lovász’s path-removal conjecture
open: For every \(k\), does some \(f(k)\) ensure that every \(f(k)\)-connected graph and prescribed vertices \(x,y\) admit an induced \(x\)-\(y\) path whose vertex deletion leaves a \(k\)-connected graph?
status: Proposed in 1975. Initial cases are solved. Kawarabayashi–Lee–Reed–Wollan establish a weaker edge-removal statement in 2008.
why: Asks whether sufficiently robust connectivity can absorb any prescribed connecting route.
key_works: Chen–Gould–Yu (2003), *Graph connectivity after path removal*; Kawarabayashi et al. (2008), [*A weaker version of Lovász’ path removal conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2007.11.003).

title: Kriesell’s Steiner-tree packing conjecture
open: If every edge cut separating a terminal set \(T\) has size at least \(2k\), must there be \(k\) edge-disjoint trees each spanning \(T\)? Nonterminal vertices may be shared.
status: Proposed in 2003. DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto prove that \(5k+4\) terminal connectivity suffices; the factor-two threshold remains open.
why: Extends spanning-tree packing to redundant terminal networks.
key_works: DeVos–McDonald–Pivotto (2016), [*Packing Steiner Trees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.7621).

title: Laborde–Payan–Xuong stable-set conjecture
open: Does every digraph have an independent vertex set meeting every longest directed path?
status: Proposed in 1983. Havet proves the conjecture when the independence number is at most two; further structured classes are known.
why: Would supply a strong structural relationship between independent sets and extremal directed paths.
key_works: Laborde–Payan–Xuong (1983), *Independent sets and longest directed paths in digraphs*; Havet (2004), *Stable set meeting every longest path*, and [author’s problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/stable_set_meeting_all_longest_directed_paths).

title: Bang-Jensen–Yeo strong spanning decomposition conjecture
open: Does an absolute \(k\) exist such that every \(k\)-arc-connected digraph contains two arc-disjoint strongly connected spanning subdigraphs?
status: Formulated in 2004. The existence assertion holds for tournaments and other special classes but remains open for general digraphs.
why: Asks whether sufficiently redundant directed connectivity always separates into two independently functioning spanning networks.
key_works: Bang-Jensen–Yeo (2004), *Decomposing \(k\)-arc-strong tournaments into strong spanning subdigraphs*; Havet’s [research problem statement](https://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/arc_disjoint_strongly_connected_spanning_subdigraphs).

title: Linear Ramsey growth for hypercubes
open: Is \(R(Q_d)\le C2^d\) for an absolute constant \(C\)?
status: Burr–Erdős, 1970s. Tikhomirov proves \(R(Q_d)=O(2^{(2-c)d})\), with \(c=0.03656\) permissible. The conjectured exponent one remains open.
why: Tests whether symmetry can keep Ramsey growth linear despite unbounded maximum degree.
key_works: Burr–Erdős (1975), *On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs*; Tikhomirov (2024), [*A remark on the Ramsey number of the hypercube*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14568).

title: Exact value of \(R(3,10)\)
open: Is \(R(3,10)=40\) or \(41\)? Equivalently, does a triangle-free 40-vertex graph with independence number at most nine exist?
status: The first unresolved entry of the classical \(R(3,t)\) sequence. Angeltveit’s 2024 revision proves the upper bound 41; the lower bound is 40.
why: A sharply bounded frontier for exhaustive graph classification and certified nonexistence.
key_works: Exoo (1989), *On two classical Ramsey numbers*; Angeltveit (2024), [*\(R(3,10)\le41\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00392).

title: Exponential dependence on maximum degree in Ramsey’s theorem
open: Prove \(R(H)\le2^{C\Delta}n\) for every \(n\)-vertex graph of maximum degree \(\Delta\), with an absolute \(C\).
status: Bounded-degree linearity dates to 1983. Exponential dependence on \(\Delta\) is necessary; the general upper bound \(2^{O(\Delta\log\Delta)}n\) retains an extra logarithm.
why: Would determine the correct degree penalty in sparse Ramsey theory.
key_works: Chvátal–Rödl–Szemerédi–Trotter (1983), *The Ramsey number of a graph with bounded maximum degree*; Conlon–Fox–Sudakov (2012), [*On two problems in graph Ramsey theory*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.0045).

title: Growth of the generalized Ramsey function \(f(n,4,3)\)
open: Determine the order of the minimum number of edge colors for \(K_n\) such that every four vertices span at least three colors.
status: Part of the Erdős–Gyárfás program. Bounds remain between \(\Omega(\log n)\) and \(\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))\).
why: Captures an intermediate regime between avoiding monochromatic cliques and requiring locally diverse colors.
key_works: Erdős–Gyárfás (1997), *A variant of the classical Ramsey problem*; Mubayi (1998), *Edge-coloring cliques with three colors on all 4-cliques*; Conlon–Fox–Lee–Sudakov (2015), [*The Erdős–Gyárfás problem on generalized Ramsey numbers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.0250).

title: Ordinary Turán density of the broken tetrahedron
open: Is \(\pi(K_4^{(3)-})=2/7\), where \(K_4^{(3)-}\) consists of three triples on four vertices?
status: Frankl–Füredi constructions give \(2/7\); upper bounds remain slightly larger. The ordinary density remains open, despite solved codegree and uniform-density variants.
why: One of the smallest hypergraphs whose extremal density is still unknown.
key_works: Frankl–Füredi (1984), *An exact result for 3-graphs*; Falgas-Ravry–Pikhurko–Vaughan–Volec (2023), [*The codegree threshold of \(K_4^-\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09396); Piga–Schülke (2026), [*Hypergraphs with arbitrarily small codegree Turán density*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.02876).

title: Extremal number of the cube graph
open: Determine the asymptotic order of \(\operatorname{ex}(n,Q_3)\).
status: Erdős–Simonovits proved \(O(n^{8/5})\) in 1970. \(C_4\)-free constructions provide \(\Omega(n^{3/2})\); the exponent remains unsettled.
why: The cube is a small symmetric bipartite graph for which standard extremal methods still leave an exponent gap.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1970), *Some extremal problems in graph theory*; [author problem archive](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/TuranCube.html); Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

title: Erdős–Simonovits odd-cycle compactness
open: For every finite family \(\mathcal F\) of bipartite graphs, does forbidding \(\mathcal F\) and all sufficiently short odd cycles recover asymptotically the extremal number of \(\mathcal F\)-free bipartite graphs?
status: Proposed in 1982. Strong versions are proved for smooth bipartite families, including several complete bipartite cases; arbitrary finite families remain open.
why: Asks whether finitely many odd-cycle exclusions can reproduce a global bipartiteness constraint.
key_works: Erdős–Simonovits (1982), *Compactness results in extremal graph theory*; Allen–Keevash–Sudakov–Verstraëte (2014), [*Turán numbers of bipartite graphs plus an odd cycle*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3805).

title: Tuza’s saturation-limit conjecture
open: For every fixed graph \(F\) with an edge, does \(\operatorname{sat}(n,F)/n\) converge? Here saturation means \(F\)-free, but adding any missing edge creates \(F\).
status: Tuza, 1986. Calbet–Freschi’s 2026 paper repairs a gap in a classical partial theorem. Finite forbidden families can have nonconvergent ratios; the singleton case remains open.
why: Would establish a stable asymptotic density for minimal saturation.
key_works: Calbet–Freschi (2026), [*The Asymptotic Behaviour of \(\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)\)*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10847).

title: Subdivision exponent-halving conjecture
open: For every fixed bipartite \(F\), does \(\operatorname{ex}(n,F)=O(n^{1+\alpha})\) imply \(\operatorname{ex}(n,\operatorname{sub}(F))=O(n^{1+\alpha/2})\), where every edge is subdivided once?
status: Kang–Kim–Liu, 2018. The predicted behavior is established for subdivisions of complete bipartite graphs, but the universal implication remains open.
why: Predicts a general transformation law for Turán exponents.
key_works: Kang–Kim–Liu (2021), [*On the rational Turán exponents conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06916); Conlon–Janzer–Lee (2021), [*More on the extremal number of subdivisions*](https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/sqbep-vc039).

title: Linear density of \(k\)-quasiplanar graphs
open: For every fixed \(k\), must an \(n\)-vertex topological graph with no \(k\) pairwise crossing edges have at most \(C_kn\) edges?
status: Conjectured in the 1990s. Linear bounds hold for small \(k\); general bounds retain logarithmic or slightly larger factors.
why: Tests whether excluding a fixed crossing clique controls density almost as strongly as planarity.
key_works: Fox–Pach–Suk (2013), [*The number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2361); Suk–Walczak (2016), [*New bounds on the maximum number of edges in \(k\)-quasi-planar graphs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.0395).

title: Sharp star chromatic number of planar graphs
open: Determine the smallest \(C\) such that every planar graph has a proper vertex coloring with \(C\) colors and no bichromatic four-vertex path.
status: Albertson and collaborators proved \(10\le C\le20\) in 2004. The general planar gap remains open.
why: Determines the cost of requiring every pair of color classes to induce a star forest.
key_works: Albertson–Chappell–Kierstead–Kündgen–Ramamurthi (2004), [*Coloring with no 2-colored \(P_4\)’s*](https://doi.org/10.37236/1779); West, [*Star colorings and acyclic colorings*](https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/starcol.html).

title: A positive Schur rule for arbitrary LLT polynomials
open: Find a uniform combinatorial rule for every Schur coefficient of an LLT polynomial indexed by an arbitrary tuple of skew diagrams, using nonnegative \(q\)-weights.
status: Algebraic Schur positivity is known. Direct coefficient rules exist for restricted shapes and graph families; the unrestricted positive rule remains missing.
why: Could explain substantial parts of Macdonald positivity and improve coefficient computation.
key_works: Lascoux–Leclerc–Thibon (1997), *Ribbon tableaux, Hall–Littlewood functions, quantum affine algebras, and unipotent varieties* (verify); Wang (2025), [*Expanding the unicellular LLT polynomials of two-headed melting lollipops into ribbon Schurs*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08187).

title: Schur positivity of Macdonald cumulants
status: Dołęga, 2017. Polynomiality, monomial and fundamental positivity, and hook Schur coefficients are known.
why: Isolates connected contributions concealed inside individual Macdonald polynomials.
key_works: Dołęga (2017), [*Macdonald cumulants, \(G\)-inversion polynomials and \(G\)-parking functions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02656).

title: Schur positivity of LLT cumulants
open: Prove that every LLT cumulant of a colored tuple of skew shapes, in Dołęga–Kowalski’s normalization, has Schur coefficients in \(\mathbb N[q]\).
status: Conjectured in 2022. Monomial and fundamental positivity, hook coefficients, vertical-shape results, and melting-lollipop cases are established.
why: Would imply Macdonald-cumulant Schur positivity through a positive expansion.
key_works: Dołęga–Kowalski (2022), [*LLT Cumulants and Graph Coloring*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.12676), [journal version](https://doi.org/10.37236/10977).

title: Goulden–Jackson Matchings–Jack positivity
open: Prove that Jack connection coefficients \(c_{\mu,\nu}^{\lambda}(1+b)\), in the triple-Cauchy normalization, lie in \(\mathbb N[b]\), and explain them using a nonnegative statistic on matchings.
status: Open since 1996. Polynomiality and top-degree positivity are known; further labeled cases were established in 2024.
why: Would explain the interpolation between symmetric-group class algebra and double-coset algebra.
key_works: Goulden–Jackson (1996), [*Connection coefficients, matchings, maps and combinatorial conjectures for Jack symmetric functions*](https://uwaterloo.ca/math/sites/default/files/uploads/documents/gjtams1996.pdf); Burchardt (2021), [*The Top-Degree Part in the Matchings-Jack Conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09330).

title: Falling-factorial positivity for shifted Jack polynomials
open: Prove that \(\alpha^{\ell(\mu)-1}H_\mu P_\mu^\#(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) is nonnegative in the basis
status: Alexandersson–Féray, 2017. Computational evidence and special cases exist; no general shifted Knop–Sahi-type rule is known.
why: Would explain positivity at partition arguments and support positive multiplication recurrences.
key_works: Alexandersson–Féray (2017), [*Shifted symmetric functions and multirectangular coordinates of Young diagrams*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.02447).

title: Thrall’s higher Lie multiplicity problem
open: Find a positive Schur-multiplicity rule for every higher Lie module \(\mathcal L_\lambda=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{m_i}(\mathcal L_i)\), where \(m_i\) counts parts of size \(i\) and \(\mathcal L_i\) is the degree-\(i\) free Lie module.
status: Thrall, 1942. Individual homogeneous free Lie pieces have a major-index rule; arbitrary higher products remain unresolved.
why: Would explain the PBW decomposition of the tensor algebra at the irreducible level.
key_works: Armon–Swanson (2025), [*Super major index and Thrall’s problem*](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.421); Adin–Roichman–Tsilevich (2025), [*Asymptotics of higher Lie characters*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.12904).

title: Macdonald filling conjugation exchanging inversion and major index
open: Construct a content-preserving bijection from fillings of shape \(\mu\) to fillings of \(\mu'\) exchanging the Haglund–Haiman–Loehr statistics \(\operatorname{inv}\) and \(\operatorname{maj}\).
status: The polynomial identity is proved. Hooks and specialized cases have bijections; the general construction remains open.
why: Would directly explain conjugate-shape symmetry between different local statistics.
key_works: Haglund–Haiman–Loehr (2005), *A combinatorial formula for Macdonald polynomials*; Gillespie–Kaliszewski–Morse (2016), [*Macdonald symmetry at \(q=1\) and a new class of inv-preserving bijections on words*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.04973).

title: Content-preserving parking-function \(q,t\)-symmetry
open: Construct an explicit bijection on word parking functions preserving label content and exchanging area with dinv, for every content.
status: The shuffle theorem establishes the generating-function equality. The uniform bijection remains open; this labeled problem strengthens unlabelled \(q,t\)-Catalan symmetry.
why: Would expose diagonal-coinvariant symmetry on its combinatorial objects.
key_works: Carlsson–Mellit (2018), *A proof of the shuffle conjecture*; Gillespie (2020), [*Two \(q,t\)-symmetry problems in symmetric function theory*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/01/12/two-qt-symmetry-problems-in-symmetric-function-theory/), OPAC-029.

title: Asymptotic sign balance in symmetric-group character tables
open: Among nonzero irreducible character-table entries of \(S_n\), does the proportion of positive entries tend to \(1/2\)?
status: Miller’s 2017 computations suggest this balance. Hopkins’s 2025 discussion retains the question; zero-density and divisibility results do not determine the conditional sign distribution.
why: Seeks a global cancellation law in a fundamental family of representation-theoretic data.
key_works: Miller (2017), [*Note on parity and the irreducible characters of the symmetric group*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.03267); Hopkins (2025), [*Maximizing negative entries in symmetric group character tables*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2025/05/02/maximizing-negative-entries-in-symmetric-group-character-tables/).

title: Schur positivity of monomial immanants of Jacobi–Trudi matrices
open: Prove that every monomial immanant of a Jacobi–Trudi matrix is a Schur-positive symmetric function.
status: Stembridge’s 1992 conjecture remains in Shareshian–Wachs’s 2026 survey. Known results for ordinary irreducible-character immanants do not establish the monomial assertion.
why: Links total positivity, Hecke characters, and Hessenberg geometry.
key_works: Haiman (1993), [*Hecke algebra characters and immanant conjectures*](https://web.math.berkeley.edu/~mhaiman/ftp/heckeimm/jams1.pdf); Shareshian–Wachs (2026), [*Combinatorics and Hessenberg varieties*](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781003145127-9).

title: Enumeration of the type-\(B\) Bruhat completion
open: Determine a uniform formula, recurrence, or effectively solvable generating function for the number of elements in the Bruhat MacNeille completion of \(B_n\).
status: Known initial counts are \(2,10,132,4824\) for \(n=1,2,3,4\). The enumeration remains open independently of a structural model.
why: Could reveal an integrable ASM symmetry class or a new enumerative structure.
key_works: Geck–Kim (1997), *Bases for the Bruhat–Chevalley order on all finite Coxeter groups*; Hopkins (2022), [*The Dedekind–MacNeille completion of type B Bruhat order*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2022/08/02/the-dedekind-macneille-completion-of-type-b-bruhat-order/).

title: Strong Sperner property for finite Coxeter weak orders
open: Prove that, in weak order on every finite Coxeter group, the largest union of \(k\) antichains has size equal to the sum of the \(k\) largest ranks.
status: Gaetz–Gao settle type \(A\) via a combinatorial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-action. The extension to all finite Coxeter groups remains conjectural.
why: Would determine sharp extremal bounds for incomparable collections throughout reflection-group orders.
key_works: Gaetz–Gao (2020), [*A combinatorial \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-action and the Sperner property for the weak order*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.05501).

title: Dyer’s complete-lattice conjecture for extended weak order
open: Prove that the inclusion poset of biclosed subsets of the positive real roots of any Coxeter group is a complete lattice. Biclosed means both the set and its complement are closed under positive roots in two-root nonnegative spans.
status: Finite and affine cases are established; general indefinite Coxeter systems remain open.
why: Would extend weak-order lattice operations to infinite reflection groups.
key_works: Dyer (2019), [*On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5557); Barkley–Speyer (2023, revised 2025), [*Affine extended weak order is a lattice*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737).

title: Dyer’s maximal-chain conjecture for biclosed sets
open: Prove that every maximal chain in extended weak order consists exactly of the initial segments of a unique total order on the positive roots.
status: Dyer’s Conjecture A. The finite and affine cases are known; the unrestricted indefinite case remains open.
why: Would identify maximal inversion chains with coherent root enumerations.
key_works: Dyer (2019), *On the Weak Order of Coxeter Groups*; Barkley–Speyer (2023, revised 2025), [*Affine extended weak order is a lattice*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05737), Conjecture 1.2 and Theorem D.

title: Log-concavity of \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials
open: For every finite labeled poset \(P\), prove that \(\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal L(P)}t^{\operatorname{des}(\pi)}\) has log-concave coefficients with no internal zeros.
status: Brenti’s conjecture survives counterexamples to Neggers–Stanley real-rootedness. Alexandersson–Jal establish stronger log-concavity for naturally labeled width-two posets.
why: Would recover robust distributional regularity after the stronger real-rootedness prediction failed.
key_works: Brenti (1989), *Unimodal, log-concave and Pólya frequency sequences in combinatorics*; Alexandersson–Jal (2024–2026), [*Rook matroids and log-concavity of \(P\)-Eulerian polynomials*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00127).

title: Central zonotopal algebras determine bridge-free graphic matroids
open: Prove that two connected loopless graphs have isomorphic central zonotopal algebras exactly when their cycle matroids become isomorphic after all bridges are deleted.
status: Nenashev classifies the external analogue in 2019. The central equivalence remains open; its Hilbert series alone is insufficient.
why: Determines how much graph structure survives in a natural finite-dimensional cut-power algebra.
key_works: Nenashev (2019), *Classification of external zonotopal algebras*; Nenashev (2020), [*Isomorphisms of zonotopal algebras*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/03/08/isomorphisms-of-zonotopal-algebras/), OPAC-032.

title: Isomorphism classification of internal zonotopal algebras
open: Give necessary and sufficient combinatorial conditions for connected graphs to have isomorphic internal zonotopal algebras, defined through cut powers with exponent \(d_I-1\).
status: Explicitly open in Nenashev’s 2020 problem list. External algebras are classified; the internal case lacks a comparable criterion.
why: Would identify which graph structures are reconstructible from interior-enumeration algebras.
key_works: Ardila–Postnikov (2010), [*Combinatorics and geometry of power ideals*](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-10-05018-X); Nenashev (2020), [*Isomorphisms of zonotopal algebras*](https://realopacblog.wordpress.com/2020/03/08/isomorphisms-of-zonotopal-algebras/).

title: The exact universal matroid correlation constant
status: Huh–Schröter–Wang prove bounds \(8/7\) and \(2\). The exact worst positive correlation remains unknown.
why: Quantifies departures from spanning-tree-like negative dependence.
key_works: Huh–Schröter–Wang (2018), [*Correlation bounds for fields and matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02675).

title: Does matroid correlation depend on the representation field?
open: Determine whether the preceding supremum, restricted to \(\mathbb F\)-representable matroids, depends on \(\mathbb F\). In particular, prove or refute \(\alpha_{\mathbb F_2}=8/7\).
status: The bounds \(8/7\le\alpha_{\mathbb F}\le2\) hold for every field; characteristic and field-size dependence remain undetermined.
why: A separation would reveal probabilistic information about representability.
key_works: Huh–Schröter–Wang (2018), [*Correlation bounds for fields and matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02675).

title: A complete excluded-minor list for \(GF(5)\)-representability
open: Determine every minor-minimal matroid not representable over \(GF(5)\), with a completeness proof.
status: Unlike the binary, ternary, and quaternary classifications, the quinary classification remains unfinished. Brettell finds 2,128 ten-element excluded minors, supplementing 564 on at most nine elements.
why: Would turn quinary representability into a concrete finite obstruction theorem.
key_works: Brettell (2025), [*The excluded minors for \(GF(5)\)-representable matroids on ten elements*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14614), [computation resources](https://homepages.ecs.vuw.ac.nz/~bretteni/research.html).

title: Complete excluded minors for dyadic matroids
open: Determine all excluded minors for matroids representable over both \(GF(3)\) and \(GF(5)\).
status: Brettell–Pendavingh enumerate excluded minors through fifteen elements and exhibit a sixteen-element obstruction. This is not yet a complete classification.
why: Would clarify the structural boundary between dyadic, near-regular, and broader quinary behavior.
key_works: Brettell–Pendavingh (2024), [*Computing Excluded Minors for Classes of Matroids Representable over Partial Fields*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13175).

title: Almost all matroids are asymmetric
open: Prove that a uniformly random labeled matroid on \(n\) elements has trivial automorphism group with probability tending to one.
status: Conjectured by Mayhew–Newman–Welsh–Whittle. Almost all matroids are either asymmetric or have automorphism group generated by one transposition; almost all sparse paving matroids are asymmetric.
why: Would justify the expected relationship between labeled and unlabeled enumeration.
key_works: Pendavingh–van der Pol (2019), [*Asymptotics of symmetry in matroids*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.04975).

title: Basis density with a non-prime-power line exclusion
open: For fixed rank \(r\), determine the limiting maximum \(b(M)/\binom nr\) among \(n\)-element matroids with no \(U_{2,t+2}\) minor when \(t\) is not a prime power; \(t=6\) is the first case.
status: Highlighted in Walsh’s 2025 problem list. Prime-power parameters have exact formulas attained by parallel blow-ups of projective geometries.
why: Isolates the effect of unavailable finite fields on extremal basis counts.
key_works: Walsh (2025), [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666), reporting joint work with van der Pol and Wigal.

title: Maximum basis density at bounded circumference
open: For every \(s\ge4\) and fixed rank \(r\), determine the limiting maximum proportion of bases in matroids with no \(U_{s,s+1}\) minor, equivalently with all circuits of size at most \(s\).
status: Explicitly open in 2025. Circumference three has an exact formula; higher circumference lacks matching constructions and upper bounds.
why: Quantifies how local circuit-size restrictions limit global independence.
key_works: Walsh (2025), [*Matroid Basis Density*](https://matroidunion.org/?p=5666).

title: Differential transcendence of \(\operatorname{Av}(4123,4231,4312)\)
open: Prove that this avoidance class’s generating function satisfies no nonzero algebraic differential equation over \(\mathbb Q(x)\).
status: Conjectured after 5,000 terms failed extensive differential-equation guessing. It remains open in the 2026 survey.
why: Could establish differential transcendence for an unusually small forbidden basis.
key_works: Albert–Homberger–Pantone–Shar–Vatter (2018), [*Generating permutations with restricted containers*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00269).

title: Are Banff and Louise quivers the same class?
open: Prove that every Banff quiver is Louise, or find a counterexample. Louise recursion adds a requirement on deletion of both endpoints of a covering pair.
status: Bucher–Machacek, OPAC-033, 2021. Ervin–Jackson resolve neighboring OPAC questions but retain Banff–Louise equality.
why: Would allow simpler Banff certificates to unlock tools for Louise cluster varieties.
key_works: Ervin–Jackson (2024), [*Answering two OPAC problems involving Banff quivers*](https://doi.org/10.5802/alco.352); the same authors (2026), [*A topology on the poset of quiver mutation classes*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.20245).

title: Shapiro’s plabic move-and-switch conjecture
open: Prove that two plabic graphs have mutation-equivalent quivers exactly when the graphs are equivalent under the prescribed local plabic moves and switches.
status: The graph-transformation-to-mutation implication is established; the converse remains open.
why: Would replace an algebraic equivalence relation with a planar geometric calculus.
key_works: Fomin–Pylyavskyy–Shustin–Thurston (2022), [*Morsifications and mutations*](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.12566), Conjecture 6.17; Fomin (2022), [OPAC slides](https://www.samuelfhopkins.com/OPAC/files/slides/fomin.pdf).

title: An exact generating function for solid partitions
open: Find a usable exact formula or closed functional characterization for \(\sum_{n\ge0}p_3(n)q^n\), where \(p_3(n)\) counts coordinatewise-decreasing three-index arrays of nonnegative integers summing to \(n\).
status: MacMahon’s natural product extension is already false at \(n=6\). Finite enumeration and simulations have advanced without a comparable general formula.
why: Would solve the first genuinely higher-dimensional partition enumeration.
key_works: Balakrishnan–Govindarajan–Prabhakar (2012), [*On the asymptotics of higher-dimensional partitions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.6231); Destainville–Govindarajan (2015), [*Estimating the asymptotics of solid partitions*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.5605).

title: The solid-partition entropy limit and constant
open: Prove convergence of \(n^{-3/4}\log p_3(n)\) and determine its limit.
status: Positive finite lower and upper bounds are proved. Limit existence was incorrectly attributed to earlier work; Dai and collaborators explicitly correct that claim. Simulations estimate \(1.822\pm0.001\).
why: Would determine the leading entropy of solid partitions and quantify departure from plane-partition behavior.
key_works: Dai–Prymak–Shadrin–Temlyakov–Tikhonov (2023), [*On the cardinality of lower sets and universal discretization*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.02113), §1.2; Destainville–Govindarajan (2015), *Estimating the asymptotics of solid partitions*.

title: Davenport’s constant for homocyclic groups of higher rank
open: Determine \(D(C_n^r)\) for composite \(n\) and \(r\ge4\), including exactly when it exceeds \(r(n-1)+1\).
status: Prime-power exponents satisfy the displayed equality. Composite exponents lack a general formula; recent counterexamples to broader bounds make individual group families essential.
why: Quantifies how interactions among primary components change zero-sum-free behavior.
key_works: Geroldinger–Liebmann–Philipp (2010/2012), [*On the Davenport constant and on the structure of extremal zero-sum free sequences*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.5835); Geroldinger–Yang (2026), *On a classical zero-sum invariant*.

title: Intermediate-length inverse zero-sum conjecture
open: For \(2\le k\le n-2\), must every length-\(2n-2+k\) sequence in \(C_n^2\), with no nonempty zero sum of length at most \(2n-1-k\), have form \(e_1^{[n-1]}e_2^{[n-1]}(e_1+e_2)^{[k]}\) for a basis?
status: Grynkiewicz–Liu reduce the problem to prime moduli. Significant prime-power ranges and moduli with no prime factor above seven are established.
why: Interpolates between inverse Davenport and short-zero-sum endpoint theorems.
key_works: Grynkiewicz–Liu (2021/2022), [*A Multiplicative Property for Zero-Sums I*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10300), [*II*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10309).

title: Gao’s relation between short zero sums and EGZ constants
open: Prove \(s(G)=\eta(G)+\exp(G)-1\) for every finite abelian group, where \(s\) forces a zero sum of exact exponent length and \(\eta\) one of positive length at most the exponent.
status: Formulated by 2003. The lower bound is elementary; equality holds in rank at most two and numerous higher-rank families.
why: Would reduce exact-length obstructions to a short-subsequence invariant.
key_works: Gao (2003), *On zero-sum subsequences of restricted size II*; Girard–Zotova (2025), [*The Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv constant of rank-two-like \(p\)-groups*](https://hal.science/hal-05333905v1/document).

title: Exact three-dimensional EGZ constants
open: Prove or refute \(s(C_n^3)=8n-7\) for even \(n\), and \(s(C_n^3)=9n-8\) for odd \(n\ge3\).
status: These values are construction lower bounds. Equality is known for powers of two and important odd families, including \(n=3^a5^b\).
why: Is the first dimension beyond the solved planar Kemnitz theorem.
key_works: Gao–Schmid (2007), [*On short zero-sum subsequences II*](https://www.math.univ-paris13.fr/~schmid/personal/schmid_16.pdf); Edel–Elsholtz–Geroldinger–Kubertin–Rackham (2007), [*Zero-sum problems in finite abelian groups and affine caps*](https://www.yvesedel.de/Papers/EEGKR.pdf).

title: Exact four-dimensional EGZ constants at odd exponents
open: Is \(s(C_n^4)=20n-19\) for every odd \(n\ge3\)?
status: Proposed with affine-cap constructions in 2007. The lower bound holds for all odd \(n\); equality holds for powers of three.
why: Connects exact-length zero sums with higher-dimensional finite-geometric caps.
key_works: Edel–Elsholtz–Geroldinger–Kubertin–Rackham (2007), [*Zero-sum problems in finite abelian groups and affine caps*](https://www.yvesedel.de/Papers/EEGKR.pdf).

title: Little cross-number conjecture
open: For \(G\cong\bigoplus_i C_{p_i^{a_i}}\), is the maximum of \(\sum_{g\in S}1/\operatorname{ord}(g)\) over zero-sum-free sequences equal to \(\sum_i(1-p_i^{-a_i})\)?
status: The Krause–Zahlten prediction holds for \(p\)-groups and many mixed-prime families; arbitrary primary combinations remain open.
why: Measures zero-sum complexity while accounting for element orders.
key_works: Kim (2014/2015), [*The Cross Number of Minimal Zero-sum Sequences in Finite Abelian Groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6867); Bashir–Schmid (2024), [*Sets of Cross Numbers of Sequences over Finite Abelian Groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07138).

title: Large cross-number conjecture
open: Is the maximum cross number of a minimal nonempty zero-sum sequence over \(G\) equal to \(1/\exp(G)+\sum_i(1-p_i^{-a_i})\)?
status: Known for \(p\)-groups and substantial mixed-prime families, including \(H_p\oplus C_{q^m}\) and \(C_p\oplus C_q\oplus C_r\) for distinct primes.
why: Determines the largest weighted size of an indecomposable zero-sum relation.
key_works: Kim (2014/2015), [*The Cross Number of Minimal Zero-sum Sequences in Finite Abelian Groups*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.6867); Bashir–Schmid (2024), *Sets of Cross Numbers of Sequences over Finite Abelian Groups*.

title: Girard’s tiny-zero-sum conjecture in rank two
open: Let \(t(G)\) force a nonempty zero-sum subsequence with cross number at most one. Prove \(t(G)=\eta(G)\) for every rank-two finite abelian group.
status: Conjectured in 2012. Additional families were proved in 2022, including certain \(C_n^2\) determined by their smallest prime divisor and number of prime factors. Higher-rank equality is false.
why: Asks when a short zero sum can simultaneously be economical in element orders.
key_works: Gao–Hui–Li–Qin–Yin (2022), [*On tiny zero-sum sequences over finite abelian groups*](https://doi.org/10.4064/cm8607-9-2021).

title: Rodney’s duplex conjecture
open: Does every Latin square of order \(n\ge2\) contain \(2n\) cells meeting each row, column, and symbol exactly twice?
status: Open since the 1980s. Every group table has a duplex; arbitrary quasigroups remain unresolved.
why: Would provide a balanced structure even when no transversal exists.
key_works: Vaughan-Lee–Wanless (2003), [*Latin Squares and the Hall–Paige Conjecture*](https://doi.org/10.1112/S0024609302001613); Wanless (2007), [*Transversals in Latin Squares*](https://www.dcs.gla.ac.uk/~pat/cpM/jchoco/latinSquares/papers/transversurveyQRSfin.pdf).

title: Wanless’s maximum duplex decomposition conjecture
open: Partition every even-order Latin square into duplexes, and every odd-order Latin square into duplexes plus one transversal.
status: A strengthening of Rodney’s conjecture. Known for all solvable group tables and small orders; finding a single duplex does not establish a complete decomposition.
why: Would organize the entire square into balanced experimental blocks.
key_works: Wanless (2002), *A generalisation of transversals for Latin squares*; Wanless (2007), [*Transversals in Latin Squares*](https://www.dcs.gla.ac.uk/~pat/cpM/jchoco/latinSquares/papers/transversurveyQRSfin.pdf).

title: Van Rees’s maximal 3-subsquare conjecture
open: If an order-\(n\) Latin square contains \(n^2(n-1)/18\) order-three subsquares, must \(n\) be a power of three?
status: The expression is a proved upper bound. For \(n>1\), equality requires \(n\equiv3\pmod6\) and corresponds to loops whose every isotope has exponent three.
why: Tests whether abundant tiny subsquares force global algebraic structure.
key_works: Kinyon–Wanless (2011), [*Loops with exponent three in all isotopes*](https://cs.du.edu/~mathfiles/preprints/nsm-math-preprint-1104.pdf).
aliases: Order conjecture for van Rees loops.

title: Exact number of reduced Latin squares of order twelve
open: Compute the exact number \(R_{12}\) of Latin squares whose first row and column are \(1,\ldots,12\), with an independently checkable enumeration.
status: Exact enumeration reaches eleven:
why: Extends a major benchmark for counting highly constrained arrays.
key_works: McKay–Wanless (2005), [*On the number of Latin squares*](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.2101); Stones (2010), *The many formulae for the number of Latin rectangles*.

title: Rapid mixing of the Jacobson–Matthews Latin-square chain
open: Prove mixing to total-variation error \(\varepsilon\) in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), uniformly over starting states.
status: Ergodicity is known since 1996; a polynomial mixing bound remains unavailable. Other exact sampling methods do not establish this chain’s guarantee.
why: Would justify efficient uniform Latin-square generation quantitatively.
key_works: Jacobson–Matthews (1996), [*Generating uniformly distributed random latin squares*](https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1520-6610(1996)4:6%3C405::AID-JCD3%3E3.0.CO;2-J); DeSalvo (2015), [*Exact sampling algorithms for Latin squares and Sudoku matrices via probabilistic divide-and-conquer*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.00235).

title: Sharp logarithmic constant for binary strength-three covering arrays
open: Determine \(c_3\) in \(\operatorname{CAN}(3,k,2)=(c_3+o(1))\log_2 k\), or establish the correct asymptotic formulation if a leading constant fails to exist.
status: Logarithmic order is known, but construction and lower-bound constants do not match.
why: Determines the irreducible number of tests covering every binary three-way interaction.
key_works: Kleitman–Spencer (1973), *Families of \(k\)-independent sets*; Sarkar–Colbourn (2016/2017), [*Upper bounds on the size of covering arrays*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.07809).

title: Existence of a projective plane of order twelve
open: Construct or exclude a symmetric \(2\!-\!(157,13,1)\) design.
status: Twelve is the smallest unsettled plane order. Akiyama–Suetake–Tanaka’s 2023 theorem restricts a possible collineation group to order one, two, or three.
why: A construction would disprove the prime-power order conjecture; exclusion would advance finite-plane classification.
key_works: Akiyama–Suetake–Tanaka (2023), [*Projective planes of order 12 do not have a collineation group of order 4*](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcd.21869).

title: Hamada’s minimum-rank conjecture
open: Among designs with the parameters of a fixed projective- or affine-geometry design over \(\mathbb F_{p^e}\), prove that the geometric design minimizes incidence-matrix rank over \(\mathbb F_p\).
status: Proposed in 1973. Several binary and low-dimensional cases are known. The stronger uniqueness assertion is false; minimum rank itself remains open.
why: Relates finite geometry to the minimum dimension of incidence-generated codes.
key_works: Hamada (1973), *On the \(p\)-rank of the incidence matrix of a balanced or partially balanced incomplete block design and its applications to error correcting codes*; Tonchev (2011), [*Finite geometry designs, codes, and Hamada’s conjecture*](https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/math-fp/98/).

title: Exact maximum period of binary orientable sequences
open: Is there a unified theory or closed-form formula for M_n, the exact maximum period of a binary orientable sequence of window length n, for all n? A periodic binary sequence is orientable when no two length-n windows are cyclic shifts of one another up to reversal, so that an observer seeing a single window can determine both its position on the cycle and the direction of travel. Exact M_n is known only for small n (computed by search/construction); the general pattern, even a provably tight lower-bound construction family, is open.
status: Introduced by Dai, Martin, and Stinson (around 2001) in the study of sequences for robotic localization (reading a cyclic track of markers with unknown orientation). Known values of M_n for small n come from explicit constructions and exhaustive/backtracking computations; constructions give good lower bounds but no exact general formula or unified asymptotic theory is known (verify current exact range — recent computational work may have extended known values).
why: Motivated by robot self-localization on cyclic tracks (position + orientation from one window read); the combinatorial core is an interesting de Bruijn-style packing problem under the reversal-equivalence constraint, where the classic 2^n de Bruijn period is unattainable and the exact achievable period resists general characterization.
key_works: Z.-D. Dai, K. Martin, D. R. Stinson, "Orientable sequences", ~2001 (verify venue: Congressus Numerantium / cryptography-and-coding proceedings); H. Fredricksen, "A survey of full length nonlinear shift register cycle algorithms", SIAM Review 1975 (de Bruijn background); recent arXiv work on computing/constructing maximum-period orientable sequences (verify); related: de Bruijn sequences B(2,n) of period 2^n; universal cycles (Chung–Diaconis–Graham 1992).
aliases: orientable sequence maximum period; M_n for orientable sequences; de Bruijn sequences with reversal constraint.
